It was also said it is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "And say: it is the truth from your Lord," that is, what was mentioned of the Qur'an, faith, and the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said it is nominative as the subject, with its predicate being "from your Lord." The meaning of the verse: Say, O Muhammad, to those whose hearts We made heedless of Our remembrance: O people, the truth is from your Lord, and to Him belongs success and abandonment, and in His hand is misguidance and guidance; He guides whom He wills to believe, and misguides whom He wills to disbelieve. [[In the Isfahan copy: "then let him disbelieve." (Marginal note of the Isfahan copy.)]] Nothing of that is up to me. I am not driving away the believers for your sake. If you wish, believe; and if you wish, disbelieve. For if you disbelieve, your Lord has prepared for your disbelief a fire whose enclosure surrounds you; and if you believe and obey, then for you is what God, Mighty and Majestic, has described for the people of His obedience.

His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ is not a permission or choice; rather it is a warning and threat, like His saying: ﴿Do what you will.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever God wills faith for, believes, and whoever God wills disbelief for, disbelieves. This is His saying: ﴿And you do not will, except that God wills.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have prepared﴾: We prepared and made ready, from "al-'utad," which is equipment. ﴿For the wrongdoers﴾: for the disbelievers, ﴿a Fire﴾. In it is evidence that the Fire is created, for if it were not created and existing and prepared, the one who informed would be a liar, and God is exalted above that.

His saying: ﴿Its enclosure surrounds them﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The enclosure of the Fire is four walls, thick, each one a distance of forty years." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/298.]] [71]

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is a wall of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: it is a neck that comes out of the Fire and encircles the disbelievers like an enclosure. Al-Qutaybi said: the "saradiq" is the chamber that surrounds the tent. Ru'bah said:

"O Hakam ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud... the enclosure of glory is extended over you."

Salamah ibn Jandal said:

"He is the one who admitted al-Nu'man into a house whose roof is... the chests of elephants, after a tent that is enclosed."

Here it means the smoke that will surround the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, which God mentioned in Surat al-Mursalat: ﴿Proceed to a shadow of three branches.﴾ [[Surat al-Mursalat: 30.]]

﴿And if they seek relief﴾ from the intensity of thirst, ﴿they will be given relief with water like molten brass﴾.

Abu Muslim narrated from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿water like molten brass﴾, he said: "Like the dregs of oil; when it is brought near to him, the skin of his face falls off into it." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/71.]] [72] Ibn 'Abbas said: thick water like the sediment of oil. al-A'mash said: it is the residue of oil. Mujahid said: pus and blood. al-Dahhak said: al-muhl is black water, and Hell is black, its water is black, its trees are black, and its people are black. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that is melted from the substances of the earth.

Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a vessel of gold and silver was presented to Ibn Mas'ud. He ordered a trench to be dug in the ground, then fuel of good firewood was thrown in, then that vessel was thrown into it. When it foamed and melted, he said to his servant: "Call whoever is present from the people of Kufa." He called a group, and when they entered upon him, he said: "Do you see this?" They said: "Yes." He said: "We have never seen in this world anything more similar to al-muhl than this gold and silver when it foamed and melted." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-muhl is that whose heat has reached its extreme.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: I heard al-Muntaji' ibn Nabhan mention a man, and he said: "He is more hateful to me than al-tulya and al-muhl." I said to him: "What is al-muhl?" He said: "It is a crust that is cut from the sides of the bread by fire, bright red, very red, as if it were a pomegranate; it is a live coal." Al-tulya: the she-camel smeared with tar. ﴿It scorches the faces.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the people of the Fire become hungry, they seek relief from the tree of Zaqqum, and they eat from it, and their skins and faces are peeled off, so that if a passerby came who knew them, he would recognize their faces by the skins of their faces in it. Then thirst overtakes them, and they seek relief, and they are given relief with ﴿water like molten brass﴾, which is that whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen, is roasted by its heat. ﴿Wretched is the drink, and evil is the Fire as a resting place﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: a dwelling. Mujahid: a gathering place. 'Ata': a place of rest. It was said: a cushion. al-Qutaybi said: a seat. The root of "murtafaq" is a reclining place; it is said of it: "irtafaqtu" when I leaned on a reclining place. The poet said:

"She said to him, and he leaned, 'Ah, is there a youth who drives the people with the gazelles of the forenoon?'" [[Jami' al-Bayan: 15/300.]]

It is also said: "irtafaqa al-rajul," when a man spends the night on his elbow, unable to sleep. Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali said:

"The one free of care slept, and I spent the night leaning on my elbow, as if in my eyes is bitter aloe that has been slaughtered." [[Jami' al-Bayan: 15/301; Lisan al-'Arab: 4/397, where it reads "mushtajiran" instead of "murtafiqan."]]

That is, cut off from its support. The "sabb" is a tree which, when uprooted, exudes something like milk, and sometimes a speck rises from it, which falls into the eye, so that it is like a spark of fire, and sometimes weakens the sight. It may also be that His saying "murtafaqan" comes from "rifq," meaning kindness and benefit.

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work.﴾ His saying "Indeed, We do not waste" is not the predicate of "Indeed, those who believe," but rather a parenthetical statement, and the predicate of the first "inna" (the one at the beginning of the verse) is His saying: ﴿those will have gardens of perpetual residence﴾. Similar to this in speech is common; the poet said:

"Indeed the Caliph—indeed God has clothed him with the garment of kingship, by which the endings are hoped for."

Some said: there is an omission in it, for its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—then indeed We do not waste their reward but reward them.﴾

Then He mentioned the reward, saying: ﴿those will have gardens of perpetual residence﴾, which is an abiding dwelling. ﴿Beneath them rivers will flow﴾. ﴿They will be adorned﴾: they will wear therein ﴿bracelets﴾, which is the plural of "aswar." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: each one of them will be adorned with three bracelets: one of silver, one of gold, and one of pearls and rubies. ﴿of gold﴾. ﴿And they will wear green garments of fine silk﴾, which is what is thin of brocade, ﴿and brocade﴾, which is what is thick of it. It was said: it is a Persian word that has been Arabized. ﴿Reclining therein﴾: in the gardens ﴿on couches﴾, which are thrones in canopies, the singular of which is "arikah." ﴿How excellent the reward, and how good the resting place﴾ — meaning the gardens.

And say not of anything, "I will surely do that tomorrow," without adding, "if God wills." ﴿And say not of anything, "I will surely do that tomorrow," unless God wills.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this means that when you resolve to do something tomorrow, or swear an oath about something, you should say, "I will do that tomorrow, if God wills." And if you forget the exception and then remember it, say it even after a year. This is a discipline from God to His Prophet (ﷺ), when he was asked about three matters: the People of the Cave, the Spirit, and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and he promised to inform them without adding the exception.

'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Maqri narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A servant's faith is not complete until he makes the exception [[i.e., until he says, "If God wills"]] in every statement he makes." [68]

﴿And remember your Lord when you forget.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan said: its meaning is: when you forget the exception and then remember, make the exception. 'Ikrimah said: its meaning is: remember your Lord when you become angry.

'Abd al-Samad ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Wuhayb, who said: It is written in the Gospel: "Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, and I will remember you when I am angry, and I will not destroy you among those who are destroyed. And when you are wronged, do not seek vengeance, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself." Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: this refers to the prayer, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it." [[Sunan al-Darimi: 1/280.]] [69]

The people of allusion (ahl al-isharah, Sufi interpreters) said: its meaning is ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ other than Him, because the remembrance of God Most High is realized only after forgetting other things. This is supported by the saying of Dhu al-Nun al-Misri: "Whoever remembers God with true remembrance forgets everything in comparison with His remembrance; and when he forgets everything in comparison with His remembrance, God preserves everything for him, and it becomes his substitute for everything." It was also said: its meaning is: remember your Lord when you abandon His remembrance, and forgetting is abandoning.

﴿And say: "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to right guidance than this."﴾ That is, He will keep me on a path nearer to Him, so I will be guided. It was also said: the meaning is, perhaps God will guide and direct me to something nearer than what I promised you and told you would happen, if He wills. It was also said: God commanded him to remember Him whenever he forgets something, and to ask Him to make him remember, so that he recalls, or to guide him to what is better for him than recalling what he forgot.

It is said that when the people asked him about the story of the People of the Cave, out of obstinacy, God commanded him to inform them that God would give him proofs and clear evidence of the truth of his prophethood and of the truth to which he called them, and would guide them to what they asked. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, did so, when He gave him knowledge of the unseen matters of the messengers and their news, which was clearer as proof and closer to right guidance than the story of the People of the Cave. Some of them said: this is something he was commanded to say along with ﴿unless God wills﴾ when he remembers the exception after forgetting it. So when a person forgets, God gives him [[so in the manuscript facsimile]] from that. Its expiation is to say: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to right guidance than this.﴾

﴿And they remained﴾, that is, the People of the Cave, ﴿in their cave﴾. Some said: this is a report about the People of the Scripture, that they said this, and they said: if it were a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, about the exact duration of their stay in the cave, then His saying ﴿Say: God knows best how long they remained﴾ would have no understandable sense, and He had already informed His creatures of the length of their stay. This is the view of Qatadah.

It is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And they said: they remained in their cave." Mutar al-Warraq said regarding this verse: this is something the Jews said, and God refuted them, saying: ﴿Say: God knows best how long they remained.﴾ Others said: this is God's report about the exact duration of their stay in the cave. They said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Say: God knows best﴾ is that the People of the Scripture said in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "For the youths, from the time they entered the cave until today, is three hundred and nine years." God, Mighty and Majestic, refuted that, saying: ﴿Say: God knows best how long they remained﴾ after He took their souls, until today. None knows that except God and whomever God has informed of it. Al-Kalbi said: the Christians of Najran said: "As for the three hundred, we know it, but as for the nine, we have no knowledge of them," so it was revealed: ﴿God knows best how long they remained.﴾

"Three hundred years" in the genitive construction without tanwin, was recited by Hamzah and al-Kisa'i; the others recite it with tanwin, meaning: and they remained in their cave three hundred years. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: the revelation came ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred [years]﴾ and they said: "Days or years?" So it was revealed, "years" (sinin), and therefore He said "years" and did not say "year." ﴿And they added nine.﴾ ﴿Say: God knows best how long they remained. His is the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clearly He sees and hears!﴾ That means: how much God sees everything that exists! And how much He hears everything that is heard! ﴿They have no protector besides Him﴾, that is, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth have no protector apart from God, ﴿no helper﴾: a supporter. ﴿And He does not share His command with anyone﴾, [meaning] among the idols or others.

﴿And recite﴾, that is, read, O Muhammad, ﴿what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, and follow what is in it. ﴿None can alter His words﴾. Al-Kalbi said: none can change the Qur'an. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: that is, none can change what He has threatened with His words against the people of disobedience and those who oppose His Book. ﴿And you will never find, other than Him, a refuge﴾, if you do not follow the Qur'an and oppose it. Ibn 'Abbas said: a shelter. al-Hasan said: a place of entry. It was said: a place of deviation. It was said: a refuge. Mujahid said: a shelter; its root is from inclining, and from it comes the word "lahd" (the niche of a grave).

﴿And restrain yourself﴾ – the verse –

The exegetes said: it was revealed concerning 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari, because he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) before this verse was revealed, and with him were Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, 'Ammar, 'Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Mihja' and Salman. Salman was wearing a cloak in which he had been sweating, and in his hand was a palm frond which he was splitting and weaving. 'Uyaynah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Does the smell of these people not bother you? By God, their smell has harmed us." He said: "We are the masters and nobles of Mudar. If we embrace Islam, the people will embrace Islam; and if we refuse, the people will refuse. Nothing prevents us from following you except these people. So remove them, until we follow you, and make for us a gathering and for them a gathering."

Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And restrain yourself﴾, that is, hold yourself ﴿with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾: who worship their Lord and honor Him, ﴿seeking His face﴾, that is, seeking God, Mighty and Majestic, not seeking any worldly gain. What is meant is good deeds and abandoning showing off. Qatadah said: that means the dawn and afternoon prayers. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Him in whose hand my soul is, they are the people of the obligatory prayers. Qatadah said: this verse was revealed concerning the People of the Suffah, who were seven hundred poor men who kept to the mosque of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), not returning to trade, nor to crops, nor to livestock; they would pray one prayer and wait for another.

Qatadah said: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to God who has placed in my community those with whom I was commanded to be patient." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 2/383.]] [70]

﴿And let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾: do not turn your eyes away from them toward others, ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾, meaning sitting with the leaders, the rich, and the nobles.

The meaning of the verse: ﴿And let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾, desiring worldly adornment, while they are immersed in seeking forgiveness, because that would be a judgment against the Prophet (ﷺ) for desiring this world. ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾, that is, whose heart We left and made forget Our remembrance. Abu al-'Aliyah said: this means Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. Others said: it means 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn. ﴿And he followed his desire, and his affair was [ever] neglect﴾. Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: lost. Dawud said: regret. Habbab said: destruction. Ibn Zayd said: opposing the truth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: excess. al-Akhfash said: exceeding the limit. al-Farra' said: abandoned. It was said: vain. Abu Zayd al-Balkhi said: going ahead in evil. Abu 'Ubayd said: it comes from the saying of the Arabs: "a horse, a fars-fart," when it outruns the other horses; and "the word of mine was farat," meaning it preceded. It was also said: its meaning is that he wasted his affair and left his days idle. They said: the believer is one who uses his time, and time does not use him.

﴿And say: the truth is from your Lord﴾. "The truth" is nominative as a quotation (hikayah). It was also said it is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "And say: it is the truth from your Lord," that is, what was mentioned of the Qur'an, faith, and the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said it is nominative as the subject, with its predicate being "from your Lord." The meaning of the verse: Say, O Muhammad, to those whose hearts We made heedless of Our remembrance: O people, the truth is from your Lord, and to Him belongs success and abandonment, and in His hand is misguidance and guidance; He guides whom He wills to believe, and misguides whom He wills to disbelieve. [[In the Isfahan copy: "then let him disbelieve." (Marginal note of the Isfahan copy.)]] Nothing of that is up to me. I am not driving away the believers for your sake. If you wish, believe; and if you wish, disbelieve. For if you disbelieve, your Lord has prepared for your disbelief a fire whose enclosure surrounds you; and if you believe and obey, then for you is what God, Mighty and Majestic, has described for the people of His obedience.

His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ is not a permission or choice; rather it is a warning and threat, like His saying: ﴿Do what you will.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever God wills faith for, believes, and whoever God wills disbelief for, disbelieves. This is His saying: ﴿And you do not will, except that God wills.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have prepared﴾: We prepared and made ready, from "al-'utad," which is equipment. ﴿For the wrongdoers﴾: for the disbelievers, ﴿a Fire﴾. In it is evidence that the Fire is created, for if it were not created and existing and prepared, the one who informed would be a liar, and God is exalted above that.

His saying: ﴿Its enclosure surrounds them﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The enclosure of the Fire is four walls, thick, each one a distance of forty years." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/298.]] [71]

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is a wall of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: it is a neck that comes out of the Fire and encircles the disbelievers like an enclosure. Al-Qutaybi said: the "saradiq" is the chamber that surrounds the tent. Ru'bah said:

"O Hakam ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud... the enclosure of glory is extended over you."

Salamah ibn Jandal said:

"He is the one who admitted al-Nu'man into a house whose roof is... the chests of elephants, after a tent that is enclosed."

Here it means the smoke that will surround the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, which God mentioned in Surat al-Mursalat: ﴿Proceed to a shadow of three branches.﴾ [[Surat al-Mursalat: 30.]]

﴿And if they seek relief﴾ from the intensity of thirst, ﴿they will be given relief with water like molten brass﴾.

Abu Muslim narrated from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿water like molten brass﴾, he said: "Like the dregs of oil; when it is brought near to him, the skin of his face falls off into it." [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/71.]] [72] Ibn 'Abbas said: thick water like the sediment of oil. al-A'mash said: it is the residue of oil. Mujahid said: pus and blood. al-Dahhak said: al-muhl is black water, and Hell is black, its water is black, its trees are black, and its people are black. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that is melted from the substances of the earth.

Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a vessel of gold and silver was presented to Ibn Mas'ud. He ordered a trench to be dug in the ground, then fuel of good firewood was thrown in, then that vessel was thrown into it. When it foamed and melted, he said to his servant: "Call whoever is present from the people of Kufa." He called a group, and when they entered upon him, he said: "Do you see this?" They said: "Yes." He said: "We have never seen in this world anything more similar to al-muhl than this gold and silver when it foamed and melted." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-muhl is that whose heat has reached its extreme.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: I heard al-Muntaji' ibn Nabhan mention a man, and he said: "He is more hateful to me than al-tulya and al-muhl." I said to him: "What is al-muhl?" He said: "It is a crust that is cut from the sides of the bread by fire, bright red, very red, as if it were a pomegranate; it is a live coal." Al-tulya: the she-camel smeared with tar. ﴿It scorches the faces.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the people of the Fire become hungry, they seek relief from the tree of Zaqqum, and they eat from it, and their skins and faces are peeled off, so that if a passerby came who knew them, he would recognize their faces by the skins of their faces in it. Then thirst overtakes them, and they seek relief, and they are given relief with ﴿water like molten brass﴾, which is that whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen, is roasted by its heat. ﴿Wretched is the drink, and evil is the Fire as a resting place﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: a dwelling. Mujahid: a gathering place. 'Ata': a place of rest. It was said: a cushion. al-Qutaybi said: a seat. The root of "murtafaq" is a reclining place; it is said of it: "irtafaqtu" when I leaned on a reclining place. The poet said:

"She said to him, and he leaned, 'Ah, is there a youth who drives the people with the gazelles of the forenoon?'" [[Jami' al-Bayan: 15/300.]]

It is also said: "irtafaqa al-rajul," when a man spends the night on his elbow, unable to sleep. Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali said:

"The one free of care slept, and I spent the night leaning on my elbow, as if in my eyes is bitter aloe that has been slaughtered." [[Jami' al-Bayan: 15/301; Lisan al-'Arab: 4/397, where it reads "mushtajiran" instead of "murtafiqan."]]

That is, cut off from its support. The "sabb" is a tree which, when uprooted, exudes something like milk, and sometimes a speck rises from it, which falls into the eye, so that it is like a spark of fire, and sometimes weakens the sight. It may also be that His saying "murtafaqan" comes from "rifq," meaning kindness and benefit.

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work.﴾ His saying "Indeed, We do not waste" is not the predicate of "Indeed, those who believe," but rather a parenthetical statement, and the predicate of the first "inna" (the one at the beginning of the verse) is His saying: ﴿those will have gardens of perpetual residence﴾. Similar to this in speech is common; the poet said:

"Indeed the Caliph—indeed God has clothed him with the garment of kingship, by which the endings are hoped for."

Some said: there is an omission in it, for its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—then indeed We do not waste their reward but reward them.﴾

Then He mentioned the reward, saying: ﴿those will have gardens of perpetual residence﴾, which is an abiding dwelling. ﴿Beneath them rivers will flow﴾. ﴿They will be adorned﴾: they will wear therein ﴿bracelets﴾, which is the plural of "aswar." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: each one of them will be adorned with three bracelets: one of silver, one of gold, and one of pearls and rubies. ﴿of gold﴾. ﴿And they will wear green garments of fine silk﴾, which is what is thin of brocade, ﴿and brocade﴾, which is what is thick of it. It was said: it is a Persian word that has been Arabized. ﴿Reclining therein﴾: in the gardens ﴿on couches﴾, which are thrones in canopies, the singular of which is "arikah." ﴿How excellent the reward, and how good the resting place﴾ — meaning the gardens.

And present to them the parable of two men... ﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾ [the Arabic word] رَجُلَيْنِ is in the accusative as the object, in the sense of: "And present to them a parable like the parable of two men." It was revealed concerning two brothers from the people of Makkah, from the Banu Makhzum. One of them was a believer, Abu Salamah Abdullah ibn Abd al-Asad ibn Abd Ya'lil, who had been the husband of Umm Salamah before the Prophet (ﷺ). The other was a disbeliever, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad ibn Abd Ya'lil. It is also said that it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and the polytheists of Makkah. It is also said that this is a parable for Uyaynah ibn Husayn and his companions, and concerning Salman and his companions. [Allah] likened them to two brothers from the Children of Israel: one a believer, whose name was Yahudha according to Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil said Tamlikha; and the other a disbeliever, whose name was Fitrus, and Wahb said Qitfir. These are the two whom Allah described in Surat al-Saffat. Their story is as follows [what Abu Amr al-Furati informed us: Muhammad ibn Imran narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Hayyan ibn Musa narrated to us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of] [[From the Isfahan manuscript; in the adopted manuscript it is replaced by: "what was narrated."]] Ma'mar, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani, who said: There were two partners, and they had eight thousand dinars. It is also said that they inherited it from their father, and they were brothers who divided it. One of them went and bought land for a thousand dinars. His companion said: "O Allah, if so-and-so has bought land for a thousand dinars, then I buy from You land in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity.

Then his companion built a house for a thousand dinars. The first said: "So-and-so has built a house for a thousand dinars, and I have bought from You a house in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he married a woman and spent a thousand dinars on her, and he said: "So-and-so has married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I propose to You for a woman of the women of Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and he said: "So-and-so has bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and I buy from You servants and goods in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity.

Then a severe need befell him, and he said: "If I went to this companion of mine, perhaps he would grant me some kindness." So he sat for him on his path until he passed by him with his retinue. He rose to him, and the other looked at him and recognized him and said: "So-and-so?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What is your condition?" He said: "A need has befallen me since you left, so I came to you that you might bestow some good upon me." He said: "Then what has become of your wealth, for we divided one wealth, and you took half of it and I took half?" So he related to him his story. He said: "And are you truly among those who believe this," meaning that you will be resurrected and recompensed? "Go away; by Allah, I will not give you anything."

So he drove him away. Then it was decreed for them both that they died, and concerning them was revealed ﴿So some of them turned to others, asking one another﴾ up to His words ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾. And there was revealed ﴿And present to them the parable of two men, for one of whom We had made two gardens of grapevines﴾: gardens of grapevines, ﴿and We had surrounded them with palm trees﴾: We had enclosed them with palm trees, ﴿and We had placed between them crops﴾, meaning:

We placed the palm trees around the grapevines, and the crops in the midst of the grapevines.

﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce﴾: gave, meaning: each one of the two gardens gave. Therefore it did not say "they both gave." ﴿Its produce﴾: its fruit complete, ﴿and did not fail therein in anything﴾, meaning it was not diminished. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth amidst them﴾, meaning:

We split and brought forth a river in their midst.

﴿And he had fruit﴾, meaning: for Fitrus. The fruit: abundant wealth yielding every kind, plural of thimar. Whoever reads thamar is reading it as the plural of thamarah. Mujahid said: gold and silver. Ibn Abbas said: kinds of wealth. Qatadah said: all kinds of wealth. Ibn Zayd said: the thamar is the principal [wealth]. ﴿He said to his companion, the believer, while he was disputing with him﴾, answering him: ﴿I am more than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾, meaning in clan and kin. Qatadah said: servants and attendants. Muqatil said: children. Its confirmation is His saying, ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children...﴾

﴿And he entered his garden﴾, meaning Fitrus, taking his brother, the Muslim, by the hand, walking him around and showing him it, and being impressed by it, ﴿while he was a wrongdoer to himself﴾ through his disbelief. When he saw what was in it of rivers, trees, flowers and fruits, he said: ﴿I do not think that this will ever perish﴾. ﴿And I do not think the Hour is coming﴾: the Resurrection, ﴿established﴾: imminent, existing. Then he wished for another wish from Allah despite his doubt and polytheism, and he said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it﴾, meaning better than the garden he had entered. The people of the Hijaz and Syria read ﴿minhuma﴾ (from both of them) in the dual form, meaning the two gardens, and so it is in their codices. ﴿A destination﴾: a place and a return.

He says: He did not give me this garden in this world except that I have with Him something better in the Hereafter.

His companion, the Muslim, said to him while disputing with him: ﴿Do you disbelieve in He who created you﴾, meaning He created your father and your origin ﴿from dust, then from a sperm-drop﴾, meaning the water of the man and the woman, ﴿then fashioned you into a man﴾, meaning He made you proportionate, a complete human male. ﴿But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾. He says: As for me, I do not disbelieve in my Lord; ﴿but as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it; its implied meaning is: "But Allah is my Lord." Others said: its original form is "lakin ana" (but I), so the hamza was dropped seeking lightness because of its frequent use, one of the two nuns was assimilated into the other, and the alif of "ana" was dropped in connected speech. Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read ﴿lakinna﴾ with the alif pronounced in connection, like the saying of the poet:

I am the sword of the tribe, so know me,
Praiseworthy, I have bared the hump [of the camel]...

There is no disagreement about its affirmation in pause. ﴿And I do not associate anyone with my Lord﴾. ﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: "What Allah wills, there is no power except in Allah"﴾. The word ﴿ma﴾ (what) is in the nominative position, meaning: it is "what Allah wills." It is permissible that it be in the accusative position, by the verb "shā'a" (willed) falling upon it. It is also said that its response is implied, and its meaning is: "What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur."

[Abu Amr al-Furati informed us: al-Qasim ibn Kulayb: al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duwri: Hajjaj: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Yamamah ibn Abdullah ibn Anas] [[Addition from the Isfahan manuscript.]] on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sees something and is impressed by it, and says: 'What Allah wills; there is no power except in Allah,' it will not harm him." [73] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/109.]]

Then he said: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾, "I am a support," and therefore it is in the accusative. ﴿Then perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and send upon it [a calamity] from heaven, [so it becomes] a barren ground, slippery﴾. ﴿Husbanan﴾ means: [a torment] from the sky. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: a punishment. Ibn Abbas said: fire. Ibn Zayd said: a decree from Allah, mighty and majestic, which He decrees. Al-Akhfash and al-Qutaybi said: a projectile from the sky, its singular being husbanah. ﴿So it becomes a barren ground, slippery﴾. Qatadah said: meaning a smooth ground with no vegetation on it. Mujahid said: sand and dust. Ibn Abbas said: it is like the mud. ﴿Or its water becomes sunken﴾, meaning vanished, disappearing into the earth, not reachable by hands, nor by buckets or ropes. Al-ghawr (sunken) is a verbal noun placed in the position of a noun, as one says: sawm, zawr, adl. And "nisā' Nūḥ" (the women of Nuh) is used for singular and dual, masculine and feminine alike. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

Its horses keep wailing over him,
Their reins hung with ornaments in rows.

And another said:

Pour forth tears of blood for them,
O hyenas, and wail for them standing.

﴿So you will not be able to seek it [again]﴾ after it has gone and been lost.

﴿And his fruit was encompassed﴾, meaning the destruction encompassed the fruits of his two gardens, and these are all kinds of fruit. Mujahid said: they were gold and silver. That is because Allah sent fire upon them, destroyed them, and their water sank. ﴿So the owner of it, the disbeliever, began to wring his hands﴾: he struck one hand upon the other, and the turning of the hands over, back and front, is from regret and anguish ﴿over what he had spent upon it﴾, meaning: over it, like His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾, meaning upon them. ﴿And it was fallen upon its trellises﴾: fallen upon its roofs, empty of its planting and its buildings. ﴿And he said: "Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾

The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And he had no company to help him﴾, meaning a group who would support him ﴿against Allah﴾: to protect him from the punishment of Allah. ﴿And he was not one who could defend himself﴾: unable to resist and avenge.

﴿There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth﴾, meaning: in the Resurrection. Al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read al-wilayah with a kasra on the waw, meaning the sovereignty and the command. The rest read it with a fatha on the waw, from the notion of allegiance (muwalah), like His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾, and His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾.

Al-Qutaybi said: he means: they will take Allah as their protector that day, and believe in Him, and disown what they used to worship. As for His saying, ﴿al-Haqq﴾ (the Truth): Abu Amr and al-Kisa'i raised it as an attribute of al-wilayah. Its confirmation is the reading of Ubayy: "There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth." The others read it with a kasra, as an attribute of Allah, like His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Lord﴾. Its confirmation is the reading of Abdullah: "There, the authority belongs to Allah, and He is the Truth," making it an attribute of Allah. ﴿He is best in reward﴾ for His friends and the people of His obedience, ﴿and best in outcome﴾ for them in the Hereafter when they return to Him. Al-'uqb (outcome) means the final result. It is said: "This is the outcome of his affair," meaning: its final end.

And present to them the parable of two men... ﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾ [the Arabic word] رَجُلَيْنِ is in the accusative as the object, in the sense of: "And present to them a parable like the parable of two men." Then a severe need befell him, and he said: "If I went to this companion of mine, perhaps he would grant me some kindness." So he sat for him on his path until he passed by him with his retinue. He rose to him, and the other looked at him and recognized him and said: "So-and-so?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What is your condition?" He said: "A need has befallen me since you left, so I came to you that you might bestow some good upon me." He said: "Then what has become of your wealth, for we divided one wealth, and you took half of it and I took half?" So he related to him his story. He said: "And are you truly among those who believe this," meaning that you will be resurrected and recompensed? "Go away; by Allah, I will not give you anything."

So he drove him away. Then it was decreed for them both that they died, and concerning them was revealed ﴿So some of them turned to others, asking one another﴾ up to His words ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾. And there was revealed ﴿And present to them the parable of two men, for one of whom We had made two gardens of grapevines﴾: gardens of grapevines, ﴿and We had surrounded them with palm trees﴾: We had enclosed them with palm trees, ﴿and We had placed between them crops﴾, meaning:

We placed the palm trees around the grapevines, and the crops in the midst of the grapevines.

﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce﴾: gave, meaning: each one of the two gardens gave. Therefore it did not say "they both gave." ﴿Its produce﴾: its fruit complete, ﴿and did not fail therein in anything﴾, meaning it was not diminished. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth amidst them﴾, meaning:

We split and brought forth a river in their midst.

﴿And he had fruit﴾, meaning: for Fitrus. The fruit: abundant wealth yielding every kind, plural of thimar. Whoever reads thamar is reading it as the plural of thamarah. Mujahid said: gold and silver. Ibn Abbas said: kinds of wealth. Qatadah said: all kinds of wealth. Ibn Zayd said: the thamar is the principal [wealth]. ﴿He said to his companion, the believer, while he was disputing with him﴾, answering him: ﴿I am more than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾, meaning in clan and kin. Qatadah said: servants and attendants. Muqatil said: children. Its confirmation is His saying, ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children...﴾

﴿And he entered his garden﴾, meaning Fitrus, taking his brother, the Muslim, by the hand, walking him around and showing him it, and being impressed by it, ﴿while he was a wrongdoer to himself﴾ through his disbelief. When he saw what was in it of rivers, trees, flowers and fruits, he said: ﴿I do not think that this will ever perish﴾. ﴿And I do not think the Hour is coming﴾: the Resurrection, ﴿established﴾: imminent, existing. Then he wished for another wish from Allah despite his doubt and polytheism, and he said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it﴾, meaning better than the garden he had entered. The people of the Hijaz and Syria read ﴿minhuma﴾ (from both of them) in the dual form, meaning the two gardens, and so it is in their codices. ﴿A destination﴾: a place and a return.

He says: He did not give me this garden in this world except that I have with Him something better in the Hereafter.

His companion, the Muslim, said to him while disputing with him: ﴿Do you disbelieve in He who created you﴾, meaning He created your father and your origin ﴿from dust, then from a sperm-drop﴾, meaning the water of the man and the woman, ﴿then fashioned you into a man﴾, meaning He made you proportionate, a complete human male. ﴿But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾. He says: As for me, I do not disbelieve in my Lord; ﴿but as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it; its implied meaning is: "But Allah is my Lord." Others said: its original form is "lakin ana" (but I), so the hamza was dropped seeking lightness because of its frequent use, one of the two nuns was assimilated into the other, and the alif of "ana" was dropped in connected speech. Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read ﴿lakinna﴾ with the alif pronounced in connection, like the saying of the poet:

I am the sword of the tribe, so know me,
Praiseworthy, I have bared the hump [of the camel]...

There is no disagreement about its affirmation in pause. ﴿And I do not associate anyone with my Lord﴾. ﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: "What Allah wills, there is no power except in Allah"﴾. The word ﴿ma﴾ (what) is in the nominative position, meaning: it is "what Allah wills." It is permissible that it be in the accusative position, by the verb "shā'a" (willed) falling upon it. It is also said that its response is implied, and its meaning is: "What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur."

[Abu Amr al-Furati informed us: al-Qasim ibn Kulayb: al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duwri: Hajjaj: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Yamamah ibn Abdullah ibn Anas] [[Addition from the Isfahan manuscript.]] on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sees something and is impressed by it, and says: 'What Allah wills; there is no power except in Allah,' it will not harm him." [73] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/109.]]

Then he said: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾, "I am a support," and therefore it is in the accusative. ﴿Then perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and send upon it [a calamity] from heaven, [so it becomes] a barren ground, slippery﴾. ﴿Husbanan﴾ means: [a torment] from the sky. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: a punishment. Ibn Abbas said: fire. Ibn Zayd said: a decree from Allah, mighty and majestic, which He decrees. Al-Akhfash and al-Qutaybi said: a projectile from the sky, its singular being husbanah. ﴿So it becomes a barren ground, slippery﴾. Qatadah said: meaning a smooth ground with no vegetation on it. Mujahid said: sand and dust. Ibn Abbas said: it is like the mud. ﴿Or its water becomes sunken﴾, meaning vanished, disappearing into the earth, not reachable by hands, nor by buckets or ropes. Al-ghawr (sunken) is a verbal noun placed in the position of a noun, as one says: sawm, zawr, adl. And "nisā' Nūḥ" (the women of Nuh) is used for singular and dual, masculine and feminine alike. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

Its horses keep wailing over him,
Their reins hung with ornaments in rows.

And another said:

Pour forth tears of blood for them,
O hyenas, and wail for them standing.

﴿So you will not be able to seek it [again]﴾ after it has gone and been lost.

﴿And his fruit was encompassed﴾, meaning the destruction encompassed the fruits of his two gardens, and these are all kinds of fruit. Mujahid said: they were gold and silver. That is because Allah sent fire upon them, destroyed them, and their water sank. ﴿So the owner of it, the disbeliever, began to wring his hands﴾: he struck one hand upon the other, and the turning of the hands over, back and front, is from regret and anguish ﴿over what he had spent upon it﴾, meaning: over it, like His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾, meaning upon them. ﴿And it was fallen upon its trellises﴾: fallen upon its roofs, empty of its planting and its buildings. ﴿And he said: "Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾

The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And he had no company to help him﴾, meaning a group who would support him ﴿against Allah﴾: to protect him from the punishment of Allah. ﴿And he was not one who could defend himself﴾: unable to resist and avenge.

﴿There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth﴾, meaning: in the Resurrection. Al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read al-wilayah with a kasra on the waw, meaning the sovereignty and the command. The rest read it with a fatha on the waw, from the notion of allegiance (muwalah), like His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾, and His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾.

Al-Qutaybi said: he means: they will take Allah as their protector that day, and believe in Him, and disown what they used to worship. As for His saying, ﴿al-Haqq﴾ (the Truth): Abu Amr and al-Kisa'i raised it as an attribute of al-wilayah. Its confirmation is the reading of Ubayy: "There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth." The others read it with a kasra, as an attribute of Allah, like His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Lord﴾. Its confirmation is the reading of Abdullah: "There, the authority belongs to Allah, and He is the Truth," making it an attribute of Allah. ﴿He is best in reward﴾ for His friends and the people of His obedience, ﴿and best in outcome﴾ for them in the Hereafter when they return to Him. Al-'uqb (outcome) means the final result. It is said: "This is the outcome of his affair," meaning: its final end.

And present to them the parable of two men... ﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾ [the Arabic word] رَجُلَيْنِ is in the accusative as the object, in the sense of: "And present to them a parable like the parable of two men." It was revealed concerning two brothers from the people of Makkah, from the Banu Makhzum. One of them was a believer, Abu Salamah Abdullah ibn Abd al-Asad ibn Abd Ya'lil, who had been the husband of Umm Salamah before the Prophet (ﷺ). The other was a disbeliever, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad ibn Abd Ya'lil. It is also said that it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and the polytheists of Makkah. It is also said that this is a parable for Uyaynah ibn Husayn and his companions, and concerning Salman and his companions. [Allah] likened them to two brothers from the Children of Israel: one a believer, whose name was Yahudha according to Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil said Tamlikha; and the other a disbeliever, whose name was Fitrus, and Wahb said Qitfir. These are the two whom Allah described in Surat al-Saffat. Their story is as follows [what Abu Amr al-Furati informed us: Muhammad ibn Imran narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Hayyan ibn Musa narrated to us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of] [[From the Isfahan manuscript; in the adopted manuscript it is replaced by: "what was narrated."]] Ma'mar, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani, who said: There were two partners, and they had eight thousand dinars. It is also said that they inherited it from their father, and they were brothers who divided it. One of them went and bought land for a thousand dinars. His companion said: "O Allah, if so-and-so has bought land for a thousand dinars, then I buy from You land in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity.

Then his companion built a house for a thousand dinars. The first said: "So-and-so has built a house for a thousand dinars, and I have bought from You a house in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he married a woman and spent a thousand dinars on her, and he said: "So-and-so has married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I propose to You for a woman of the women of Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and he said: "So-and-so has bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and I buy from You servants and goods in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity.

Then a severe need befell him, and he said: "If I went to this companion of mine, perhaps he would grant me some kindness." So he sat for him on his path until he passed by him with his retinue. Ibn Abbas said: kinds of wealth. Qatadah said: all kinds of wealth. Qatadah said: servants and attendants. Muqatil said: children. Its confirmation is His saying, ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children...﴾

﴿And he entered his garden﴾, meaning Fitrus, taking his brother, the Muslim, by the hand, walking him around and showing him it, and being impressed by it, ﴿while he was a wrongdoer to himself﴾ through his disbelief. When he saw what was in it of rivers, trees, flowers and fruits, he said: ﴿I do not think that this will ever perish﴾. ﴿And I do not think the Hour is coming﴾: the Resurrection, ﴿established﴾: imminent, existing. Praiseworthy, I have bared the hump [of the camel]...

[73] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/109.]]

Then he said: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾, "I am a support," and therefore it is in the accusative. ﴿Then perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and send upon it [a calamity] from heaven, [so it becomes] a barren ground, slippery﴾. ﴿Husbanan﴾ means: [a torment] from the sky. Al-Akhfash and al-Qutaybi said: a projectile from the sky, its singular being husbanah. ﴿So it becomes a barren ground, slippery﴾. Qatadah said: meaning a smooth ground with no vegetation on it. Its horses keep wailing over him,
Their reins hung with ornaments in rows.

And another said:

Pour forth tears of blood for them,

The rest read it with a fatha on the waw, from the notion of allegiance (muwalah), like His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾, and His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾.

Al-Qutaybi said: he means: they will take Allah as their protector that day, and believe in Him, and disown what they used to worship. As for His saying, ﴿al-Haqq﴾ (the Truth): Abu Amr and al-Kisa'i raised it as an attribute of al-wilayah. Its confirmation is the reading of Ubayy: "There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth." And strike for them, O Muhammad, the parable of the life of this world, which is like water We sent down from the sky, meaning rain. The wise have said: God, exalted is He, likened this world to water, because water does not settle in one place or state, and likewise this world does not last for anyone. Water is also not constant in one condition, and so is this world. Water perishes, and so this world perishes. No one can enter water without getting wet, and likewise no one is spared the afflictions and temptations of this world. When water is in its measure, it is beneficial and sustaining, but when it exceeds its measure, it is harmful and destructive. So it is with this world: what is sufficient of it benefits, and its excess harms.

﴿And the plants of the earth mingle with it﴾, that is, with the water, ﴿and then it becomes dry stalks﴾ within a short time. Ibn 'Abbas said: dry. al-Dahhak said: broken. al-Akhfash said: crumbled, and its root meaning is breaking. ﴿Which the winds scatter﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they turn it around. Ibn Kaysan said: they bring it and take it away. al-Akhfash said: they lift it up.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they scatter it. al-Qutaybi said: they blow it away. Talha ibn Musarrif recited it and said: the wind scatters it, tadhruhu dharwan, and tadhrihi dharyan, and adhratahu idhra'an, when it carries it away. ﴿And God is ever Capable of all things﴾, meaning able.

﴿Wealth and children﴾, by which 'Uyayna and his companions among the nobles and the rich take pride, ﴿are the adornment of the life of this world﴾, and they are not provisions for the grave nor part of the reckoning of the Hereafter. ﴿But the enduring good deeds﴾, which Salman and his companions among the freedmen and the poor perform, ﴿are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope﴾, that is, better in what a person hopes for.

They differed over what the enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat) are. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrima, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: they are the servant's saying: "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest." The evidence for this is what Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated from Abu Hilal, from Qatada, that the Prophet ﷺ took a branch and shook it until its leaves fell, and said: "When the Muslim says: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest, his sins fall away from him [in the source: his sins fall away as this leaf falls]." 

"Take them to yourself, Abu al-Darda', before you are prevented from them, for they are among the treasures of Paradise and the choicest of speech, and they are the enduring good deeds." [74] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/415.]

'Uthman (may God be pleased with him), Ibn 'Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: they are "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God, the Exalted, the Mighty." The evidence for this is what al-Qasim ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Umari and Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated from 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd, from Khalid ibn 'Imran, that the Prophet ﷺ went out to his people and said: "Take your shield." They said: "O Messenger of God, is there an enemy who has come?" He said: "No, rather from the Fire." They said: "And what is our shield from the Fire?" He said: "Praise be to God, glory be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God, the Exalted, the Mighty, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection going before, guarding, and following after, and they are the enduring good deeds." [75] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 3/289.]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Increase in the enduring good deeds."

It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The community (al-milla)." It was said: "And what is it?" He said: "The magnifying of God (takbir), the declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), the glorification of God (tasbih), and there is no power nor strength except by God." [76] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/75.]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the freedman of Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, said: Salim sent me to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and said: "Tell him: meet me at the corner of the grave, for I have a need of you." He said: So they met, and one of them greeted the other. Then Salim said: "What do you count as the enduring good deeds?" He said: "There is no god but God, praise be to God, glory be to God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God." Salim said to him: "When did you add: and there is no power nor strength except by God?" 

He said: "I have always included it in them." He returned to him two or three times, and he did not desist. Salim said: "Postpone it." So I came to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and he related that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "I was taken up to the heaven, and I saw Abraham (peace be upon him), who said: 'O Gabriel, who is this with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' He welcomed me and made me at ease, then said: 'Command your community to increase their planting of Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is vast.' I said: 'And what is the planting of Paradise?' He said: 'There is no power nor strength except by God.'" [77] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/418.]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Amr ibn Sharahbil, Masruq and Ibrahim said: they are the five daily prayers, and they are good deeds that ﴿remove evil deeds﴾. [Qur'an 11:114.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the righteous deeds: "There is no god but God," "I seek God's forgiveness," and "God's blessings be upon Muhammad," and the prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, almsgiving, manumission, struggle (jihad), maintaining ties of kinship, and all good deeds that remain for their doers in Paradise for as long as the heavens and the earth endure.

'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they are good words. 'Awf said: I asked al-Hasan about the enduring good deeds, and he said: intentions and aspirations, for by them deeds are accepted and raised. Qatada said: they are everything done seeking God's face. And God knows best.

﴿And the day We set the mountains in motion﴾, that is, We remove them from their places. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited: tusayyaru (with a ta' and a fathah on the ya'), al-jibalu (in the nominative), in the passive voice. ﴿And you will see the earth laid bare﴾, manifest, as is plain to the eye, with no tree, mountain, fruit, nor anything to cover it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the small is the minor lapses, touching and kissing and intimacy; the great is fornication and full intercourse. ﴿Except that it has counted them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it has recorded their deeds. al-Suddi said: it wrote them down and preserved them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it guarded them. It is said: it numbered them. Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath said: when al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad recited this verse, he said: "By God, they were struck with fear of the minor before the major."

The Messenger of God ﷺ gave an example of minor sins, saying: "They are like a people who set out traveling until they halted in a wilderness. Each man went out to gather firewood, so one man brought a stick and another brought two sticks, until they gathered a heap and kindled a fire. They differed concerning him. Adam's sin was disobedience, and Iblis's sin was pride.

Ibn 'Abbas said in another report: he was of the jinn, and he was named after the gardens (janan), because he was a guardian over them, so he was attributed to them, just as one says of a man: Makki, Kufi, Madani, Basri. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Iblis was one of the jinn whom the angels overcame; one of the angels captured him and took him up to heaven. Qatada said: he was a jinn who went out of obedience to God, the Exalted. ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord﴾, meaning: he departed from the obedience of his Lord. Mujahid said: among Iblis's descendants are Lafis, Wallahan, who is the master of purification and prayer; al-Hafhan; Murra, by whom Iblis is also called; Zaylanun, the master of markets, who sets his banner in every market of heaven and earth; al-Dathr, the master of calamities, who commands the striking of faces, the tearing of garments, and calling for woe and war; al-A'war, the master of the doors of adultery; Mabsut, the master of news, who brings it and casts it into people's mouths, and they find no basis for it; and Dasim, who, when a man enters his house without greeting and without mentioning God's name, displays to him the ugliest things that he has not lifted or has not placed well; and when he eats without mentioning God's name over it, he eats with him.

al-A'mash said: Often I enter a house without mentioning God's name and without greeting, and I see its washing place, and I say: "Lift up!" And I dispute with them, then I remember and say: "Dasim, Dasim."

No one can enter water without getting wet, and likewise no one is spared the afflictions and temptations of this world. So it is with this world: what is sufficient of it benefits, and its excess harms.

Ibn Kaysan said: they bring it and take it away. al-Akhfash said: they lift it up.

'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they are good words. 'Awf said: I asked al-Hasan about the enduring good deeds, and he said: intentions and aspirations, for by them deeds are accepted and raised. Qatada said: they are everything done seeking God's face. And God knows best.

﴿And the day We set the mountains in motion﴾, that is, We remove them from their places. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited: tusayyaru (with a ta' and a fathah on the ya'), al-jibalu (in the nominative), in the passive voice. ﴿And you will see the earth laid bare﴾, manifest, as is plain to the eye, with no tree, mountain, fruit, nor anything to cover it. 'Ata' said: you will see the inner earth outward, with those who were in its belly brought out and standing upon its surface. ﴿And We will gather them﴾, that is, We will bring them together at the place of standing for reckoning, ﴿and leave none of them behind﴾, that is, We will not abandon nor leave anyone of them. ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾, meaning row by row, for they are a single row.

It is said: standing. It will be said to them, that is, to the disbelievers, and its wording is general while its meaning is specific: ﴿You have come to Us just as We created you the first time﴾, meaning alive. It is said: naked. It is said: unarmed. It is said: alone. ﴿Rather, you claimed that We would not appoint for you a promised time﴾, meaning the Resurrection.

Exalted is He, saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, meaning the books of the deeds of creation. ﴿And you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾, of the evil deeds, ﴿and they will say, when they see it: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great of our sins unrecorded?"﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: the small is smiling, and the great is laughing aloud. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the small is the minor lapses, touching and kissing and intimacy; the great is fornication and full intercourse. ﴿Except that it has counted them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it has recorded their deeds. al-Suddi said: it wrote them down and preserved them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it guarded them. It is said: it numbered them. Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath said: when al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad recited this verse, he said: "By God, they were struck with fear of the minor before the major."

The Messenger of God ﷺ gave an example of minor sins, saying: "They are like a people who set out traveling until they halted in a wilderness. Each man went out to gather firewood, so one man brought a stick and another brought two sticks, until they gathered a heap and kindled a fire. Indeed, a minor sin accumulates upon its doer until it destroys him." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/321.] [78]

﴿And they will find what they did present﴾, written and recorded in their book. ﴿And your Lord wrongs no one﴾, meaning: He does not diminish the reward of anyone who has done good. al-Dahhak said: He does not take anyone for a crime he did not commit, nor transfer one person's sin to another.

﴿And when We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam,"﴾ the Exalted says, reminding these arrogant people of what pride brought upon Iblis, and teaching them that it arises from enmity and envy toward them, like what was in their father's case: "And remember, O Muhammad, when We said to the angels: prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated, except Iblis, who was of the jinn." They differed concerning him. Ibn 'Abbas said: Iblis was of a tribe among the tribes of the angels called the jinn, created from the scorching fire, while the angels were created from light other than this tribe. His name in Syriac was 'Azazil and in Arabic al-Harith. He was one of the treasurers of Paradise and the chief of the angels of this world. He had authority over the lowest heaven and over the earth. He was among the angels most forbearing and most knowledgeable. He governed what lay between heaven and earth, and so he saw for himself nobility and greatness, and this is what led him to pride. He disobeyed, so God transformed him into a cursed, stoned devil. If a man's sin is due to pride, do not hope for him; if his sin is disobedience, then hope for him. Adam's sin was disobedience, and Iblis's sin was pride.

Ibn 'Abbas said in another report: he was of the jinn, and he was named after the gardens (janan), because he was a guardian over them, so he was attributed to them, just as one says of a man: Makki, Kufi, Madani, Basri. [Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Sirri informed us, from Yahya ibn 'Uthman ibn Zafar, who said:] (an addition from the Isfahan manuscript): Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning God's words, "who was of the jinn," that he said: he was of the Jananiyyun, who worked in Paradise. al-Hasan said: Iblis was never of the angels for the blink of an eye; he was the origin of the jinn just as Adam is the origin of mankind. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Iblis was one of the jinn whom the angels overcame; one of the angels captured him and took him up to heaven. Qatada said: he was a jinn who went out of obedience to God, the Exalted. ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord﴾, meaning: he departed from the obedience of his Lord. The Arabs say: the date (ruṭba) "fasaqat" when it comes out of its skin, and the mouse "fasaqat" when it comes out of its hole, and for this reason it is called al-fuwaysiqa. It is said: fisq means expansion; the Arabs say: "So-and-so fasaqa in expenditure" when he spends lavishly, and "he obtained no wealth except that he fasaqahu", meaning he destroyed and squandered it. The wicked person (fasiq) is so named because he expands in the prohibitions of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and makes them trivial for himself.

﴿Will you then take him﴾, meaning, O children of Adam, ﴿and his offspring as allies besides Me, while they are an enemy to you﴾, that is, enemies. al-Hasan said: mankind is from Adam's descendants at its end, and the jinn are from Iblis's descendants at its end. Mujahid said: among Iblis's descendants are Lafis, Wallahan, who is the master of purification and prayer; al-Hafhan; Murra, by whom Iblis is also called; Zaylanun, the master of markets, who sets his banner in every market of heaven and earth; al-Dathr, the master of calamities, who commands the striking of faces, the tearing of garments, and calling for woe and war; al-A'war, the master of the doors of adultery; Mabsut, the master of news, who brings it and casts it into people's mouths, and they find no basis for it; and Dasim, who, when a man enters his house without greeting and without mentioning God's name, displays to him the ugliest things that he has not lifted or has not placed well; and when he eats without mentioning God's name over it, he eats with him.

al-A'mash said: Often I enter a house without mentioning God's name and without greeting, and I see its washing place, and I say: "Lift up!" And I dispute with them, then I remember and say: "Dasim, Dasim."

Makhlad narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: I was sitting one day when a porter came carrying a jar, and he set it down, then came to me and said: "Are you al-Sha'bi?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Tell me: does Iblis have a wife?" I said: "That is a wedding I did not witness." Then I recalled God's words: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me?﴾ and I knew that there is no offspring except from a wife. I said: "Yes." So he took his jar and departed. He said: I thought he was a dream interpreter. Ibn Zayd said: Iblis is the father of the jinn just as Adam (peace be upon him) is the father of mankind. God said to Iblis: "I do not create for Adam any offspring except that I produce for you the like of it," [when] (in the manuscript: then) Adam begot children. Qatada said: they reproduce as the children of Adam reproduce, and every offspring of Adam is accompanied by a devil who is joined to him; there is no son of Adam except that a devil has been paired with him.

﴿How evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾, that is, how evil is the replacement for Iblis and his offspring in place of God. Qatada said: how evil is what they took in exchange for the worship of their Lord: obedience to Iblis and his offspring.

And strike for them, O Muhammad, the parable of the life of this world, which is like water We sent down from the sky, meaning rain. The wise have said: God, exalted is He, likened this world to water, because water does not settle in one place or state, and likewise this world does not last for anyone. Water is also not constant in one condition, and so is this world. Water perishes, and so this world perishes. No one can enter water without getting wet, and likewise no one is spared the afflictions and temptations of this world. When water is in its measure, it is beneficial and sustaining, but when it exceeds its measure, it is harmful and destructive. So it is with this world: what is sufficient of it benefits, and its excess harms.

﴿And the plants of the earth mingle with it﴾, that is, with the water, ﴿and then it becomes dry stalks﴾ within a short time. Ibn 'Abbas said: dry. al-Dahhak said: broken. al-Akhfash said: crumbled, and its root meaning is breaking. ﴿Which the winds scatter﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they turn it around. Ibn Kaysan said: they bring it and take it away. al-Akhfash said: they lift it up.

Abu 'Ubayda said: they scatter it. al-Qutaybi said: they blow it away. Talha ibn Musarrif recited it and said: the wind scatters it, tadhruhu dharwan, and tadhrihi dharyan, and adhratahu idhra'an, when it carries it away. ﴿And God is ever Capable of all things﴾, meaning able.

﴿Wealth and children﴾, by which 'Uyayna and his companions among the nobles and the rich take pride, ﴿are the adornment of the life of this world﴾, and they are not provisions for the grave nor part of the reckoning of the Hereafter. ﴿But the enduring good deeds﴾, which Salman and his companions among the freedmen and the poor perform, ﴿are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope﴾, that is, better in what a person hopes for.

They differed over what the enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat) are. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrima, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: they are the servant's saying: "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest." The evidence for this is what Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated from Abu Hilal, from Qatada, that the Prophet ﷺ took a branch and shook it until its leaves fell, and said: "When the Muslim says: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest, his sins fall away from him [in the source: his sins fall away as this leaf falls]." 

"Take them to yourself, Abu al-Darda', before you are prevented from them, for they are among the treasures of Paradise and the choicest of speech, and they are the enduring good deeds." [74] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/415.]

'Uthman (may God be pleased with him), Ibn 'Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: they are "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God, the Exalted, the Mighty." The evidence for this is what al-Qasim ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Umari and Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated from 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd, from Khalid ibn 'Imran, that the Prophet ﷺ went out to his people and said: "Take your shield." They said: "O Messenger of God, is there an enemy who has come?" He said: "No, rather from the Fire." They said: "And what is our shield from the Fire?" He said: "Praise be to God, glory be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God, the Exalted, the Mighty, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection going before, guarding, and following after, and they are the enduring good deeds." [75] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 3/289.]

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Increase in the enduring good deeds."

It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The community (al-milla)." It was said: "And what is it?" He said: "The magnifying of God (takbir), the declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), the glorification of God (tasbih), and there is no power nor strength except by God." [76] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/75.]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the freedman of Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, said: Salim sent me to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and said: "Tell him: meet me at the corner of the grave, for I have a need of you." He said: So they met, and one of them greeted the other. Then Salim said: "What do you count as the enduring good deeds?" He said: "There is no god but God, praise be to God, glory be to God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except by God." Salim said to him: "When did you add: and there is no power nor strength except by God?" 

He said: "I have always included it in them." He returned to him two or three times, and he did not desist. Salim said: "Postpone it." So I came to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and he related that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "I was taken up to the heaven, and I saw Abraham (peace be upon him), who said: 'O Gabriel, who is this with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' He welcomed me and made me at ease, then said: 'Command your community to increase their planting of Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is vast.' I said: 'And what is the planting of Paradise?' He said: 'There is no power nor strength except by God.'" [77] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/418.]

ما أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ (Ma ashhadtuhum): "I did not make them witness." Ma ahdartuhum: I did not bring them to attend, meaning Iblis and his offspring. It is also said: it means all the disbelievers. Al-Kalbi said: it means the angels of the heavens. Abu Ja'far recited (ma ashhadnahum) with a nun and alif, in the plural of majesty: "the creation of the heavens and the earth," so that I would seek their help in creating them, consult them and take their counsel regarding them; "nor the creation of themselves; and I would not take the misleaders as helpers" (ʿaḍudan): supporters and aides.

وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نادُوا: Hamzah recited it with a nun. The rest recite it with a ya', because of His words: شُرَكائِيَ (shurakai-ya), "My partners," and He did not say: shurakaʾunا (shurakaʾana), "our partners." شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أنهم شركائي: "My partners whom you claimed to be My partners." فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ: they called on them but they did not respond to them. وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ: We will place between them, meaning between the idols and their worshippers. It is also said: between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance, مَوْبِقاً (mawbiqan), an abyss (a gloomy separating chasm).

Abdullah ibn Umar said: it is a deep valley in Hell, by which, on the Day of Resurrection, the people of "There is no god but Allah" are separated from everyone else. Ibn Abbas said: it is a valley in the Fire. Mujahid said: a valley of boiling water (hamim). ʿIkrimah said: it is a river in the Fire that flows with fire, on whose two banks are snakes like black mules; when they hurry toward them to seize them, they cry out for rescue by plunging into the Fire from it. Al-Hasan said: enmity. Al-Dahhak and ʿAta said: destruction. Abu ʿUbayd said: a promised place, and its root is destruction. It is said: awbaqahu yubiquhu ibaqan, meaning he destroyed him; and waqiba yabiqu waqan, meaning ruin; it is said: waqiba yuwbaqu, yabiqu, and yaʾbiqu; he is wabiq and wabaq, and the verbal noun is waqb and wuqub.

وَرَأَى الْمُجْرِمُونَ: the criminals, meaning the polytheists, see the Fire, فَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مُواقِعُوها: and they think that they will be thrown into it, meaning will enter it. Mujahid said: will plunge into it. It is also said: will descend upon it and fall into it. Al-A'mash recited (mulaqquha), meaning gathered within it, and the pronoun refers to the group. وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْها مَصْرِفاً: and they will find no escape from it.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed the disbeliever sees Hell and thinks that it will fall upon him from a distance of forty years' journey." [Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/330.] [79]

وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا: We have explained in this Qur'an for the people every kind of example, so that they may remember and be admonished. وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا: man is most contentious, in false argument; it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. It is also said that it is general, not specific, and they cited what was narrated by al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knocked on his door, he and Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: Will you not pray? I said: O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah the Exalted; if He wills to raise us, He raises us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away when I said that to him and did not reply anything. I heard him striking his thigh and saying: وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا!" وَرَبُّكَ الْغَفُورُ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ: Your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of mercy. لَوْ يُؤاخِذُهُمْ بِما كَسَبُوا: Were He to take them to account for what they earned of sins, لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذابَ: He would have hastened their punishment in this world. بَلْ لَهُمْ مَوْعِدٌ: rather, they have an appointed time, which is the Day of Reckoning, لَنْ يَجِدُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ مَوْئِلًا: they will not find besides it any refuge: a place of escape and a means of deliverance. Al-A'sha said:

And I have sometimes stolen from the lord of the house in his heedlessness, and he has sometimes been wary of me, yet he does not flee.
[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/334.]

Meaning: he does not escape.

وَتِلْكَ الْقُرى أَهْلَكْناهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا: And those towns — We destroyed them when they did wrong, meaning disbelieved, وَجَعَلْنا لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ مَوْعِداً: and We set an appointed time for their destruction, meaning a term.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verse 60–82 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his servant (fatahu)... [the verse]. Ibn 'Abbas said: When Musa (peace be upon him) and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When the dwelling became settled for them, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Remind them of the Days of Allah﴾. So he addressed his people and reminded them of the good and blessings Allah the Mighty and Majestic had given them, when He saved them from the family of Pharaoh, destroyed their enemy, and made them successors in the land. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, chose me for Himself, cast upon me love from Him, and ﴿gave you of all that you asked for﴾. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave any blessing that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and making it known to them. Then a man from the Children of Israel said to him: "We have understood what you say. Is there anyone on the face of the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic was displeased with him because he did not refer knowledge to Him. He sent Jibril to him, who said: "O Musa, what do you know of where I place My knowledge? Rather, I have a servant at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas who is more knowledgeable than you." Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him that: "Go to the sea, and you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea; when you lose the fish, there you will find the righteous servant." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/349.] [80]

Ibn 'Abbas said in another narration: Musa asked his Lord, saying: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just?" He said: "The one who judges with truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?"
