*a sandy place like the hollow of the sand-grouse's nest"* [[al-Sihah: 4/1431.]]

Al-Zajjaj cited in (latakhadhta) the verse of Abu Shammam al-Sabbabi:

*"They took iron from iron as hammers,*
*whose dwellers are spirits and bodies"*

﴿For it﴾, i.e., for its repair and erection, ﴿a wage﴾: a reward and payment. It was also said: hospitality and provision.

Then the Khidr (peace be upon him) said: ﴿This is the parting between me and you.﴾ Lahiq ibn Humayd recited (firaqun) with tanwin. ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not hold patience.﴾ ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾. Ka'b said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were disabled and five of whom worked at sea.

In His words ﴿to poor people﴾ there is evidence that a poor person (miskin), even if he owns something, does not lose the designation of poverty if he has a need for something beyond what he owns, and it is permissible for him to take zakat. [Abu Bakr 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ali al-Hamshadhi informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Razi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Zakariyya al-Maqdisi, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-San'ani, from Ibrahim] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; the adopted copy has instead: "and it was narrated."]] ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: concerning His words, ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾ — they were poor while the boat was worth a thousand dinars? He said: Indeed, a traveler is poor even if he has a thousand dinars with him.

﴿So I intended to damage it, and behind them was﴾ — i.e., in front of them and ahead of them, like His words: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [[Surat Ibrahim: 16.]] and ﴿Behind them is a barrier﴾ [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 100.]], meaning in front of them. The poet said:

*"Do the sons of Marwan hope for my hearing and obedience,*
*while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me?"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/390.]]

It was also said: ﴿behind them﴾ means after them, and their return on their journey would be past it, but they did not know of its condition, so God informed the Khidr of its condition. ﴿A king who seizes every boat by force﴾, i.e., every sound boat. He relied on the context to indicate this, and what supports it is what Sufyan related from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited: (wa kana amamahum malikun yakhudhu kulla safinatin salihatin ghasban) ["and in front of them was a king who seized every sound boat by force"]. So he damaged it and made it defective, so that this king would not seize it. His name was Jalanda, and he was an unbeliever. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His name was Manawah ibn Jalanda al-Ardani. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Hadad ibn Badad.

﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared﴾ — i.e., we knew. In the codex of Ubayy: (fakhafa rabbuka), meaning he knew, and parallels to this are numerous. Qutrub said: its meaning is "we disliked," as you say: "I separated the two men out of fear that they would fight," though there is no fear in you, only dislike that they should fight. ﴿That he would overwhelm them﴾, i.e., destroy them. It was also said: cover them. Al-Kalbi said: he would burden them with rebellion and disbelief. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: We feared that his love for him would lead them to bring him into his religion.

﴿So we intended that their Lord should replace him with one better than him in purity, ﴾ i.e., righteousness and Islam, ﴿and nearer in kinship﴾. Ruhm is from kinship (rahim) and relationship (qaraba). It was also said: it is from mercy (rahmah). It is said: rahm and ruhm for mercy, like halk and halk, and 'umur and 'umur. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*"And the womb of one who bends did not bend"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 12/232.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nearer in kinship﴾ means more joined to the womb and more dutiful to his parents. Qatadah said: nearer in good. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning more merciful to them than they were toward the one slain. Al-Farra' said: ﴿and nearer that they would show mercy to him﴾. Al-Kalbi said: God replaced them with a girl, whom a prophet among the prophets married, and she bore him a prophet through whom God, Mighty and Majestic, guided a nation.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Qadi informed us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Falih, from Maymun ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qaddah, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning this verse, who said: "He replaced them with a girl, and she bore seventy prophets." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 6/376.]] [91]

Ibn Jurayj said: He replaced them with a righteous Muslim boy, whereas the one slain was an unbeliever. Likewise in the codex of Ubayy: (As for the boy, he was an unbeliever, and his parents were believers). Qatadah said: his parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved over him when he was killed; had he lived, their destruction would have been in him. So let a person be content with the decree of God, for God's decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he loves.

﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, named Asram and Sarim, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them.﴾ They differed about what that treasure was. Some of them said: it was sheets of knowledge buried beneath it; this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ibn 'Abbas said: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "It was a tablet of gold on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I marvel at one who believes in destiny, how he can grieve; I marvel at one who is certain of provision, how he can toil; I marvel at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice; I marvel at one who believes in reckoning, how he can be heedless; I marvel at one who knows the world and how it turns its people over, how he can feel at ease in it. There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/38.]]

It has also been reported from the Prophet ﷺ, in some narrations, that this saying was written on that tablet beneath what these verses mention: "O one who is anxious, you are anxious about what does not concern you. If fever seizes you, you will be feverish [....] [[Blank in the manuscript photograph.]] you have risen to a lofty height of knowledge; how can it guard you when the pen has dried?!" [92]

'Ikrimah said: That treasure was wealth.

[Abu Bakr al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Qaydus al-Ta'ra'iqi told us, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Salih al-Thaqafi [[In the Isfahan copy: al-Dimashqi. Marginal note in the manuscript.]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Yazid ibn Yusuf al-San'ani, from Yazid ibn Abi Yazid, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Makhul, from [Abu] [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis: 174; the manuscript reads: Umm.]] al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning His words ﴿and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾: "It was gold and silver." [[Zad al-Masir: 5/126.]] [93]

﴿And their father was righteous﴾. His name was Kashih, and he was among the pious. It is mentioned that the two were preserved through the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness of theirs is mentioned. Between them and the father through whom they were preserved there were seven generations. He was a wanderer.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, preserves through a righteous man his child and his child's child, his clan in which he lives, and the houses around him; they remain in God's protection and concealment.

It is related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that whenever he saw his son he would say: "My son, I shall increase my prayer for your sake, hoping that I may be protected through you," and he would recite this verse. [Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Balkhi, from Ahmad ibn al-Layth ibn al-Khalil, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Haytham ibn 'Abd Allah al-Dabi'i told me, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: My father told me, from Yahya ibn Isma'il ibn Muslimah ibn Kuhayl, who said: I had a sister older than me who became confused and lost her mind, and became withdrawn. She was in a room at the far end of the roofs, and she remained in that state for some ten-odd years. Despite losing her mind, she was eager for prayer and purity. One night while I was sleeping, the door of my house knocked at midnight. I said: "Who is this?" She said: "Bahha." I said: "My sister?" She said: "Your sister." I said: "Here I am." I got up, opened the door, and she entered; she had not come to the house for more than ten years. I said to her: "O sister, is there good?" She said: "Good. Last night I came in my dream, and it was said: 'Peace be upon you, O Bahha.' I said: 'And upon you peace.' It was said: 'Indeed God has preserved your father Isma'il ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl through your grandfather Salamah, and has preserved you through your father Isma'il. If you wish, I will pray to God for you to remove what is in you; and if you wish, you may be patient and have Paradise. For Abu Bakr and 'Umar have interceded for you with God, Mighty and Majestic, by the love your father and grandfather had for them.'" I said: "If one of the two must be chosen, then patience in what I am in, and Paradise. For God, Mighty and Majestic, is vast in His creation, and nothing is too great for Him; if He wills, He can bring both together for me." She said: "Then it was said to me: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has brought both together for you, and He is pleased with your father and grandfather for their love of Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Arise and come down.'" He said: So God removed what was in her.

﴿So your Lord intended, O Musa, that they should reach their maturity﴾, i.e., reach their full strength and power. It was also said: eighteen years. ﴿And extract their treasure﴾ that was hidden beneath the wall. ﴿And I did it not by my own command﴾, i.e., by my own opinion and of my own accord, but I did it by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not hold patience over﴾. (istaa'a) and (istaṭā'a) have the same meaning.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verse 60–82 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his servant (fatahu)... [the verse]. Ibn 'Abbas said: When Musa (peace be upon him) and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When the dwelling became settled for them, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Remind them of the Days of Allah﴾. So he addressed his people and reminded them of the good and blessings Allah the Mighty and Majestic had given them, when He saved them from the family of Pharaoh, destroyed their enemy, and made them successors in the land. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, chose me for Himself, cast upon me love from Him, and ﴿gave you of all that you asked for﴾. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave any blessing that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and making it known to them. Then a man from the Children of Israel said to him: "We have understood what you say. Is there anyone on the face of the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic was displeased with him because he did not refer knowledge to Him. He sent Jibril to him, who said: "O Musa, what do you know of where I place My knowledge? Rather, I have a servant at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas who is more knowledgeable than you." Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him that: "Go to the sea, and you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea; when you lose the fish, there you will find the righteous servant." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/349.] [80]

Ibn 'Abbas said in another narration: Musa asked his Lord, saying: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just?" He said: "The one who judges with truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people to add to his knowledge, hoping to hear a word that guides him to guidance or turns him away from ruin." He said: "If there is among Your servants one more knowledgeable than me, guide me to him." He said to him: "Yes, among My servants is one more knowledgeable than you." He said: "Who is he?" He said: "Al-Khidr." He said: "Where can I seek him?" He said: "On the coast, by the rock." And He made the fish a sign for him and said: "When this fish comes to life and lives, then your companion is there." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/343, with slight variation.] [81]

They had taken with them salted fish, and that is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when Musa, son of 'Imran, said to his servant﴾. His companion was Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Ifra'im ibn Yusuf. It was said: his fatan was the brother of Yusha', who was with him on the journey. It was said: his fatan was his servant and slave. ﴿I will not cease﴾: I will not stop walking, ﴿until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾. Qatada said: the sea of Persia and Rome on the eastern side. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Tangier. [Ibid.: 337.] Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Africa. ﴿Or I will go on for a long period (huqban)﴾; its plural is ahqab: a long time or an age. 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: a huqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: seventy years. It was said: the two seas are Musa and al-Khidr, who were two seas of knowledge.

So they took bread and a salted fish and set out until they reached the rock that is at the meeting place of the two seas at night. There was a spring there called the Water of Life; no thing touched by that water fails to come alive. When the spirit and coolness of the water touched the fish, it moved in the basket, came to life, and entered the sea. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But when they reached the meeting place between them﴾, meaning Musa and his servant, between the two seas, ﴿they forgot their fish﴾: they left their fish behind. The fish was actually with Yusha', and it was he who forgot it, but the forgetting is attributed to both of them, and the intended one is one of them, as in His saying: ﴿From them come out the pearls and coral﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 22]; these come out only from the salt water, not the fresh. This is permissible because both had taken provisions for their journey, so it is correct to attribute it to both, as one says: "The people went out to such-and-such a place, and they carried with them such-and-such provisions," though only one of them carried it; but since it was part of their affair and their decision, it is attributed to them. ﴿And it took its way into the sea in a tunnel﴾: that is, a path and a course, moving and going through it.

They differed about how this happened.
Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The water parted from the course of the fish, and it became a window that did not close. Musa entered the window following the fish's trail, and there he found al-Khidr (peace be upon him)." [82]

Ibn 'Abbas said: He saw the trace of its wing in the mud when it fell into the water, and the fish did not touch anything without it drying up until it became a rock.

Ibn 'Abbas narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When they reached the rock, they put their heads down and slept. The fish thrashed in the basket, came out of it, and fell into the sea, ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a tunnel﴾. Allah the Mighty and Majestic held back the flow of water from the fish, so over it there became like an arch. When Musa (peace be upon him) woke up, his servant forgot to tell him about the fish, and they went on the rest of that day and night, until the next day when ﴿they had passed beyond, Musa said to his servant: Bring us our morning meal﴾." [Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/182; Zad al-Masir: 5/114.] [83]

Qatada said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic returned its spirit to the fish, and it moved through the sea until it reached the sea, then it took a course; every path it took, the water became solid and dry as a path. Al-Kalbi said: Yusha' ibn Nun performed ablution from the Spring of Life, and some of that water splashed onto the salted fish in the basket, and it came to life, then leapt into that water, striking the water with its tail; whatever water it struck while moving became dry. ﴿When they had passed beyond﴾, meaning that place, Musa said to his servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾: give us our food and provisions. That was because Yusha' ibn Nun, when he saw that from the fish, got up to catch up with Musa to inform him about the matter of the fish, but he forgot to tell him. So they remained that whole day until they prayed the noon prayer the next day. Musa had not felt fatigue on that journey except that day, when he passed the place he had been commanded to reach. So he said to his servant when he grew weary and tired: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue (nasaban) from this journey of ours﴾, that is, hardship and exhaustion. That was because hunger was cast upon Musa after he passed the rock, so that he would remember the fish and return to the place he sought. His servant said, remembering: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish﴾; that is, I left it and lost it. Muqatil said: the rock is the one below the River of Oil.

It was said that there is an ellipsis in it, meaning: "I forgot to mention the matter of the fish." Then he said: ﴿And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾, meaning: Satan made me forget it, that I should not mention it. It was said that there is inversion in it, its sense being: "None but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it." ﴿And it took its way into the sea in a tunnel, wondrously﴾: it is permissible that this is the speech of Yusha', saying that the fish took its way into the sea wondrously. It was said that Yusha' said: the fish leapt into the sea and took a course in it, so I marveled greatly at that. It is also permissible that this is the speech of Musa: Yusha' said to him, "It took its way into the sea," and Musa replied, "Wondrously," as if he said: "It was a great wonder."

Ibn Zayd said: What is more wondrous than a fish that had been eaten from for ages, then came back to life until it went into the sea? He said: It was split in two. Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa took the fish's path into the sea, wondrously. Wahb said: a mark of the fish's course appeared on the water, a split and a trench like a river, from where it entered to where it ended. Musa returned until he reached the meeting place of the two seas, and there he found al-Khidr (peace be upon him). That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Musa said: That is what we were seeking﴾, that is, we were seeking, meaning al-Khidr. ﴿So they turned back, retracing their footsteps (qasasan)﴾: they followed the trace, tracking it.

﴿And they found a servant from Our servants﴾, meaning al-Khidr [[In the manuscript there is a mark of omission after it, but it does not appear in the manuscript's photograph.]], whose name was Balya ibn Malkan ibn Yaqtin; "al-Khidr" is his epithet, named so because [Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Makki ibn 'Abdan: Akhbarana Abu al-Azhar from 'Abd al-Razzaq from] [[From a second copy; the adopted copy has instead: narrated.]] Ma'mar from Hammam ibn Munabbih from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Khidr was only named al-Khidr because he sat on a white patch, and it turned green (tahtazzu) beneath him." [[In the source: "then it was trembling."]] [Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/72, no. 34048.] [84]

['Abd al-Razzaq said: a white patch means a dry grass; [and] a patch: a piece of land with vegetation.] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Mujahid said: al-Khidr was named so because whenever he prayed, what was around him turned green. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Ibn Jurayj from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, who said: Musa saw al-Khidr on a green prayer mat on the surface of the water, and he greeted him.

Ibn 'Abbas said, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Musa came to al-Khidr while he was sleeping with a cloth over him. He greeted him, and he sat up and said: 'And upon you peace, O prophet of the Children of Israel.' Musa said: 'How did you know about me? Who told you that I am the prophet of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'The One who made you known to me and guided you to me.'" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/15, with slight variation.] [85]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He reached him while he was praying, and when he finished the greeting, he said: "And how is peace in our land?!" Then they sat talking, and a swallow came and took water in its beak. Al-Khidr said: "O Musa, it occurred to you that you are the most knowledgeable person on earth. Your knowledge and the knowledge of the first and last people, in comparison with Allah, is no more than what the swallow took with its beak from the water." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they found a servant from Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾. ﴿Musa said to him: Shall I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance (rushdan)﴾:

right? He said: ﴿Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience about what you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾, meaning: about what you do not know. Ibn 'Abbas said: That was because he was a man who acted upon the unseen.

Musa said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command.﴾ He said: ﴿So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you﴾: until I begin to tell you of it and explain its matter to you. So they set out walking, seeking a ship to board. When they got on the ship, ﴿they boarded the ship﴾. The people of the ship said: "These are thieves," and they ordered them to get out. The owner of the ship said: "They are not thieves, but I see the faces of prophets."

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "They went walking along the shore of the sea. A ship passed by them, and they spoke to its people asking them to carry them. They recognized al-Khidr, and so they carried him without a fare. When they entered the sea, al-Khidr took an axe and broke a plank of the ship until the water entered it. Musa filled it with his garment and said to him: ﴿Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?﴾" [Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/39, with variation.] [86]

The people of Kufa read (liyaghraqa) with an open yaʼ and (ahluha) with a raised lam, making the verb belong to them; this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. ﴿Indeed you have done a thing (shay'an) terrible (imran)﴾, that is, something objectionable. Al-Qutaybi said: wonderful. In the language of the Arabs, al-Imr is a calamity. The rajiz said:

"The rivals have met from me a terrible thing,
a great calamity, a grave, terrible matter" [al-Sihah: 2/581.]

Its root meaning is: everything that is severe and abundant; one says "amara al-qawm" when they multiply and their matter becomes severe.

He said: ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ Musa said: ﴿Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot﴾

[Akhbarana Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq from Hamid ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Sa'd ibn Musa al-Marwarudhi said in Baghdad, and we were informed by Muhammad ibn Abi Najiyya al-Iskandarani from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna from 'Amr ibn Dinar from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] 'Ikrima from Ibn 'Abbas from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The first was from the matter of forgetting, the second was by decree, and had Musa been patient, Allah would have related to us more than He related." [87] [[Tarikh Madinat Dimashq: 61/155, ed. Dar al-Fikr.]]

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: As for him, he did not forget, but it was a form of indirect speech (ma'arid al-kalam). Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is "for what you left of your covenant." ﴿And do not burden me (turhiqni)﴾: hasten me [[Zad al-Masir: 5/120, attributing it to al-Farra'.]]. It was said: do not cover me ([[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/354.]]) ﴿with difficulty in my affair﴾: he says, do not constrict my affair and my companionship with you.

﴿So they set out until, when they met a boy﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-Khidr found boys playing, and he took a handsome, bright-faced boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. Ibn 'Abbas said: he had not yet reached puberty.

Al-Dahhak said: He was a boy who did corruption, and his parents were harmed by him; his name was Khashbud. Shu'ayb al-Hayyani said: his name was Hayshur. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: his father's name was Mulas, and his mother's name was Rahmi. Al-Kalbi said: he was a youth who cut the road, took goods, and would take refuge with his parents, who would swear on his behalf; so al-Khidr seized him, threw him down, then pulled his head from his body. Some people said: he kicked him with his foot and killed him. Others said: he struck his head against the wall and killed him.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman from Yahya ibn Qays from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed as a disbeliever [Musnad Ahmad: 5/121]. When he killed him, Musa said to him: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul without its having killed anyone?﴾" [88]

That is: pure. It was said: Muslim. Al-Kisa'i said: al-Zakiya and al-Zakiyya are two dialects, like al-Qasiya and al-Qasiyya. Abu 'Amr said: al-Zakiya is one who has never sinned at all, while al-Zakiyya is one who sinned and then repented. ﴿Without a soul﴾: that is, without his having killed a soul that required retaliation. ﴿Indeed you have done a thing (shay'an) abominable (nukra)﴾: objectionable. Qatada and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Nukr is more severe and greater than al-Imr.

He said: ﴿Did I not say to you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ He said: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this﴾, that is, this time, ﴿then do not keep company with me; you have reached from me an excuse (udhran)﴾ regarding my parting.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Makki ibn 'Abdan from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad: Akhbarana Hamza al-Zayyat from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned anyone and prayed for him, he began with himself. One day he said: "May Allah's mercy be upon us and upon my brother Musa. Had he remained with his companion, he would have seen wonders [al-'ajab] [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; the manuscript has al-a'ajib.]], but he said: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me; you have reached from me an excuse.﴾" [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/392, where it reads al-'ajib instead of al-'ajab.]] [89]

﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning Antioch. Ibn Sirin said: Ayla [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; the manuscript has al-Ayla.]], which is the farthest land of Allah from the sky. ﴿They asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them﴾, that is, to host them as guests. That is because they asked them for food and they did not feed them, and they asked for hospitality and they did not host them.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman from Yahya ibn Qays from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿but they refused to entertain them﴾, and he said: "They were a town of miserly people." [90] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/461, no. 4500.]]

Qatada said regarding this verse: the worst of towns is the one that does not host the guest and does not recognize the right of the wayfarer.

They found within it a wall, i.e., in the town, [about to fall]. Wahb said: It was a wall whose height in the sky was one hundred cubits, "about to collapse." This is figurative speech (majaz), because a wall has no will; its meaning is that it came close to and drew near that state, like the words of God Most High: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it﴾ [[Surat Maryam: 90.]]. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*"It almost did, or it intended, to slope toward the ground"* [[Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/290.]]

Some of them said: It returned to its companion, because when this state comes from one's Lord, it is His will, like the words of God Most High: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa﴾ [[Surat al-A'raf: 154.]], whereas it is actually the one who is angry who calms down. And He said: ﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾ [[Surat Muhammad: 21.]], whereas it is the people concerned who resolve. Al-Harithi said:

*"The spear desires the chest of Abu Bara'*
*and turns away from the blood of Bani 'Uqayl"* [[Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/358; Lisan al-'Arab: 3/189, where "yu'dil" appears instead of "yarghab."]]

And 'Uqayl said:

*"Indeed, a time that brings together the union of Sulayma*
*is a time that intends kindness"* [[al-Sihah: 2/661; Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/358.]]

﴿To collapse﴾, i.e., to fall and crumble. From this comes the word for the falling of stars, which is their falling and departure from their places. Yahya ibn 'Umar recited: (yurid an yanqaad), meaning it is uprooted and split. It is said: the tooth (insaddat al-sinn) split from its root. Some of the Kufans said: infiqad (inqiyad) means a split lengthwise. It is said: the wall, the tooth, and the well split (inqada) when they cracked lengthwise.

﴿And he set it up﴾: he made it straight. Ibn 'Abbas said: he demolished it, then sat down and rebuilt it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he wiped the wall and pushed it with his hand, and it became upright.

Musa said: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken﴾ [a reward for it]. Abu 'Amr recited (latakhadhta), and both are dialectal variants, like your saying (ittaba'a) and (taba'a), and (ittaqa) and (taqa). The poet said:

*"I have taken my saddle beside its stirrup,*
*a sandy place like the hollow of the sand-grouse's nest"* [[al-Sihah: 4/1431.]]

Al-Zajjaj cited in (latakhadhta) the verse of Abu Shammam al-Sabbabi:

*"They took iron from iron as hammers,*
*whose dwellers are spirits and bodies"*

﴿For it﴾, i.e., for its repair and erection, ﴿a wage﴾: a reward and payment. It was also said: hospitality and provision.

Then the Khidr (peace be upon him) said: ﴿This is the parting between me and you.﴾ Lahiq ibn Humayd recited (firaqun) with tanwin. ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not hold patience.﴾ ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾. Ka'b said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were disabled and five of whom worked at sea.

In His words ﴿to poor people﴾ there is evidence that a poor person (miskin), even if he owns something, does not lose the designation of poverty if he has a need for something beyond what he owns, and it is permissible for him to take zakat. [Abu Bakr 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ali al-Hamshadhi informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Razi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Zakariyya al-Maqdisi, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-San'ani, from Ibrahim] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; the adopted copy has instead: "and it was narrated."]] ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: concerning His words, ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾ — they were poor while the boat was worth a thousand dinars? He said: Indeed, a traveler is poor even if he has a thousand dinars with him.

﴿So I intended to damage it, and behind them was﴾ — i.e., in front of them and ahead of them, like His words: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [[Surat Ibrahim: 16.]] and ﴿Behind them is a barrier﴾ [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 100.]], meaning in front of them. The poet said:

*"Do the sons of Marwan hope for my hearing and obedience,*
*while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me?"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/390.]]

It was also said: ﴿behind them﴾ means after them, and their return on their journey would be past it, but they did not know of its condition, so God informed the Khidr of its condition. ﴿A king who seizes every boat by force﴾, i.e., every sound boat. He relied on the context to indicate this, and what supports it is what Sufyan related from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited: (wa kana amamahum malikun yakhudhu kulla safinatin salihatin ghasban) ["and in front of them was a king who seized every sound boat by force"]. So he damaged it and made it defective, so that this king would not seize it. His name was Jalanda, and he was an unbeliever. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His name was Manawah ibn Jalanda al-Ardani. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Hadad ibn Badad.

﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared﴾ — i.e., we knew. In the codex of Ubayy: (fakhafa rabbuka), meaning he knew, and parallels to this are numerous. Qutrub said: its meaning is "we disliked," as you say: "I separated the two men out of fear that they would fight," though there is no fear in you, only dislike that they should fight. ﴿That he would overwhelm them﴾, i.e., destroy them. It was also said: cover them. Al-Kalbi said: he would burden them with rebellion and disbelief. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: We feared that his love for him would lead them to bring him into his religion.

﴿So we intended that their Lord should replace him with one better than him in purity, ﴾ i.e., righteousness and Islam, ﴿and nearer in kinship﴾. Ruhm is from kinship (rahim) and relationship (qaraba). It was also said: it is from mercy (rahmah). It is said: rahm and ruhm for mercy, like halk and halk, and 'umur and 'umur. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*"And the womb of one who bends did not bend"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 12/232.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nearer in kinship﴾ means more joined to the womb and more dutiful to his parents. Qatadah said: nearer in good. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning more merciful to them than they were toward the one slain. Al-Farra' said: ﴿and nearer that they would show mercy to him﴾. Al-Kalbi said: God replaced them with a girl, whom a prophet among the prophets married, and she bore him a prophet through whom God, Mighty and Majestic, guided a nation.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Qadi informed us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Falih, from Maymun ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qaddah, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning this verse, who said: "He replaced them with a girl, and she bore seventy prophets." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 6/376.]] [91]

Ibn Jurayj said: He replaced them with a righteous Muslim boy, whereas the one slain was an unbeliever. Likewise in the codex of Ubayy: (As for the boy, he was an unbeliever, and his parents were believers). Qatadah said: his parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved over him when he was killed; had he lived, their destruction would have been in him. So let a person be content with the decree of God, for God's decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he loves.

﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, named Asram and Sarim, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them.﴾ They differed about what that treasure was. Some of them said: it was sheets of knowledge buried beneath it; this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ibn 'Abbas said: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "It was a tablet of gold on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I marvel at one who believes in destiny, how he can grieve; I marvel at one who is certain of provision, how he can toil; I marvel at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice; I marvel at one who believes in reckoning, how he can be heedless; I marvel at one who knows the world and how it turns its people over, how he can feel at ease in it. There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/38.]]

It has also been reported from the Prophet ﷺ, in some narrations, that this saying was written on that tablet beneath what these verses mention: "O one who is anxious, you are anxious about what does not concern you. If fever seizes you, you will be feverish [....] [[Blank in the manuscript photograph.]] you have risen to a lofty height of knowledge; how can it guard you when the pen has dried?!" [92]

'Ikrimah said: That treasure was wealth.

[Abu Bakr al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Qaydus al-Ta'ra'iqi told us, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Salih al-Thaqafi [[In the Isfahan copy: al-Dimashqi. Marginal note in the manuscript.]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Yazid ibn Yusuf al-San'ani, from Yazid ibn Abi Yazid, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Makhul, from [Abu] [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis: 174; the manuscript reads: Umm.]] al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning His words ﴿and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾: "It was gold and silver." [[Zad al-Masir: 5/126.]] [93]

﴿And their father was righteous﴾. His name was Kashih, and he was among the pious. It is mentioned that the two were preserved through the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness of theirs is mentioned. Between them and the father through whom they were preserved there were seven generations. He was a wanderer.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, preserves through a righteous man his child and his child's child, his clan in which he lives, and the houses around him; they remain in God's protection and concealment.

It is related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that whenever he saw his son he would say: "My son, I shall increase my prayer for your sake, hoping that I may be protected through you," and he would recite this verse. [Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Balkhi, from Ahmad ibn al-Layth ibn al-Khalil, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Haytham ibn 'Abd Allah al-Dabi'i told me, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: My father told me, from Yahya ibn Isma'il ibn Muslimah ibn Kuhayl, who said: I had a sister older than me who became confused and lost her mind, and became withdrawn. She was in a room at the far end of the roofs, and she remained in that state for some ten-odd years. Despite losing her mind, she was eager for prayer and purity. One night while I was sleeping, the door of my house knocked at midnight. I said: "Who is this?" She said: "Bahha." I said: "My sister?" She said: "Your sister." I said: "Here I am." I got up, opened the door, and she entered; she had not come to the house for more than ten years. I said to her: "O sister, is there good?" She said: "Good. Last night I came in my dream, and it was said: 'Peace be upon you, O Bahha.' I said: 'And upon you peace.' It was said: 'Indeed God has preserved your father Isma'il ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl through your grandfather Salamah, and has preserved you through your father Isma'il. If you wish, I will pray to God for you to remove what is in you; and if you wish, you may be patient and have Paradise. For Abu Bakr and 'Umar have interceded for you with God, Mighty and Majestic, by the love your father and grandfather had for them.'" I said: "If one of the two must be chosen, then patience in what I am in, and Paradise. For God, Mighty and Majestic, is vast in His creation, and nothing is too great for Him; if He wills, He can bring both together for me." She said: "Then it was said to me: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has brought both together for you, and He is pleased with your father and grandfather for their love of Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Arise and come down.'" He said: So God removed what was in her.

﴿So your Lord intended, O Musa, that they should reach their maturity﴾, i.e., reach their full strength and power. It was also said: eighteen years. ﴿And extract their treasure﴾ that was hidden beneath the wall. ﴿And I did it not by my own command﴾, i.e., by my own opinion and of my own accord, but I did it by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not hold patience over﴾. (istaa'a) and (istaṭā'a) have the same meaning.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verse 60–82 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his servant (fatahu)... [the verse]. Ibn 'Abbas said: When Musa (peace be upon him) and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When the dwelling became settled for them, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Remind them of the Days of Allah﴾. So he addressed his people and reminded them of the good and blessings Allah the Mighty and Majestic had given them, when He saved them from the family of Pharaoh, destroyed their enemy, and made them successors in the land. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, chose me for Himself, cast upon me love from Him, and ﴿gave you of all that you asked for﴾. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave any blessing that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and making it known to them. Then a man from the Children of Israel said to him: "We have understood what you say. Is there anyone on the face of the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic was displeased with him because he did not refer knowledge to Him. He sent Jibril to him, who said: "O Musa, what do you know of where I place My knowledge? Rather, I have a servant at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas who is more knowledgeable than you." Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him that: "Go to the sea, and you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea; when you lose the fish, there you will find the righteous servant." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/349.] [80]

Ibn 'Abbas said in another narration: Musa asked his Lord, saying: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just?" He said: "The one who judges with truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people to add to his knowledge, hoping to hear a word that guides him to guidance or turns him away from ruin." He said: "If there is among Your servants one more knowledgeable than me, guide me to him." He said to him: "Yes, among My servants is one more knowledgeable than you." He said: "Who is he?" He said: "Al-Khidr." He said: "Where can I seek him?" He said: "On the coast, by the rock." And He made the fish a sign for him and said: "When this fish comes to life and lives, then your companion is there." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/343, with slight variation.] [81]

They had taken with them salted fish, and that is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when Musa, son of 'Imran, said to his servant﴾. His companion was Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Ifra'im ibn Yusuf. It was said: his fatan was the brother of Yusha', who was with him on the journey. It was said: his fatan was his servant and slave. ﴿I will not cease﴾: I will not stop walking, ﴿until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾. Qatada said: the sea of Persia and Rome on the eastern side. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Tangier. [Ibid.: 337.] Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Africa. ﴿Or I will go on for a long period (huqban)﴾; its plural is ahqab: a long time or an age. 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: a huqb is eighty years. Mujahid said: seventy years. It was said: the two seas are Musa and al-Khidr, who were two seas of knowledge.

So they took bread and a salted fish and set out until they reached the rock that is at the meeting place of the two seas at night. There was a spring there called the Water of Life; no thing touched by that water fails to come alive. When the spirit and coolness of the water touched the fish, it moved in the basket, came to life, and entered the sea. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But when they reached the meeting place between them﴾, meaning Musa and his servant, between the two seas, ﴿they forgot their fish﴾: they left their fish behind. The fish was actually with Yusha', and it was he who forgot it, but the forgetting is attributed to both of them, and the intended one is one of them, as in His saying: ﴿From them come out the pearls and coral﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 22]; these come out only from the salt water, not the fresh. This is permissible because both had taken provisions for their journey, so it is correct to attribute it to both, as one says: "The people went out to such-and-such a place, and they carried with them such-and-such provisions," though only one of them carried it; but since it was part of their affair and their decision, it is attributed to them. ﴿And it took its way into the sea in a tunnel﴾: that is, a path and a course, moving and going through it.

They differed about how this happened.
Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The water parted from the course of the fish, and it became a window that did not close. Musa entered the window following the fish's trail, and there he found al-Khidr (peace be upon him)." [82]

Ibn 'Abbas said: He saw the trace of its wing in the mud when it fell into the water, and the fish did not touch anything without it drying up until it became a rock.

Ibn 'Abbas narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When they reached the rock, they put their heads down and slept. The fish thrashed in the basket, came out of it, and fell into the sea, ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a tunnel﴾. Allah the Mighty and Majestic held back the flow of water from the fish, so over it there became like an arch. When Musa (peace be upon him) woke up, his servant forgot to tell him about the fish, and they went on the rest of that day and night, until the next day when ﴿they had passed beyond, Musa said to his servant: Bring us our morning meal﴾." [Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/182; Zad al-Masir: 5/114.] [83]

Qatada said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic returned its spirit to the fish, and it moved through the sea until it reached the sea, then it took a course; every path it took, the water became solid and dry as a path. Al-Kalbi said: Yusha' ibn Nun performed ablution from the Spring of Life, and some of that water splashed onto the salted fish in the basket, and it came to life, then leapt into that water, striking the water with its tail; whatever water it struck while moving became dry. ﴿When they had passed beyond﴾, meaning that place, Musa said to his servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾: give us our food and provisions. That was because Yusha' ibn Nun, when he saw that from the fish, got up to catch up with Musa to inform him about the matter of the fish, but he forgot to tell him. So they remained that whole day until they prayed the noon prayer the next day. Musa had not felt fatigue on that journey except that day, when he passed the place he had been commanded to reach. So he said to his servant when he grew weary and tired: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue (nasaban) from this journey of ours﴾, that is, hardship and exhaustion. That was because hunger was cast upon Musa after he passed the rock, so that he would remember the fish and return to the place he sought. His servant said, remembering: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish﴾; that is, I left it and lost it. Muqatil said: the rock is the one below the River of Oil.

It was said that there is an ellipsis in it, meaning: "I forgot to mention the matter of the fish." Then he said: ﴿And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾, meaning: Satan made me forget it, that I should not mention it. It was said that there is inversion in it, its sense being: "None but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it." ﴿And it took its way into the sea in a tunnel, wondrously﴾: it is permissible that this is the speech of Yusha', saying that the fish took its way into the sea wondrously. It was said that Yusha' said: the fish leapt into the sea and took a course in it, so I marveled greatly at that. It is also permissible that this is the speech of Musa: Yusha' said to him, "It took its way into the sea," and Musa replied, "Wondrously," as if he said: "It was a great wonder."

Ibn Zayd said: What is more wondrous than a fish that had been eaten from for ages, then came back to life until it went into the sea? He said: It was split in two. Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa took the fish's path into the sea, wondrously. Wahb said: a mark of the fish's course appeared on the water, a split and a trench like a river, from where it entered to where it ended. Musa returned until he reached the meeting place of the two seas, and there he found al-Khidr (peace be upon him). That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Musa said: That is what we were seeking﴾, that is, we were seeking, meaning al-Khidr. ﴿So they turned back, retracing their footsteps (qasasan)﴾: they followed the trace, tracking it.

﴿And they found a servant from Our servants﴾, meaning al-Khidr [[In the manuscript there is a mark of omission after it, but it does not appear in the manuscript's photograph.]], whose name was Balya ibn Malkan ibn Yaqtin; "al-Khidr" is his epithet, named so because [Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Makki ibn 'Abdan: Akhbarana Abu al-Azhar from 'Abd al-Razzaq from] [[From a second copy; the adopted copy has instead: narrated.]] Ma'mar from Hammam ibn Munabbih from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Khidr was only named al-Khidr because he sat on a white patch, and it turned green (tahtazzu) beneath him." [[In the source: "then it was trembling."]] [Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/72, no. 34048.] [84]

['Abd al-Razzaq said: a white patch means a dry grass; [and] a patch: a piece of land with vegetation.] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Mujahid said: al-Khidr was named so because whenever he prayed, what was around him turned green. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Ibn Jurayj from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, who said: Musa saw al-Khidr on a green prayer mat on the surface of the water, and he greeted him.

Ibn 'Abbas said, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Musa came to al-Khidr while he was sleeping with a cloth over him. He greeted him, and he sat up and said: 'And upon you peace, O prophet of the Children of Israel.' Musa said: 'How did you know about me? Who told you that I am the prophet of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'The One who made you known to me and guided you to me.'" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/15, with slight variation.] [85]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He reached him while he was praying, and when he finished the greeting, he said: "And how is peace in our land?!" Then they sat talking, and a swallow came and took water in its beak. Al-Khidr said: "O Musa, it occurred to you that you are the most knowledgeable person on earth. Your knowledge and the knowledge of the first and last people, in comparison with Allah, is no more than what the swallow took with its beak from the water." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they found a servant from Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾. ﴿Musa said to him: Shall I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance (rushdan)﴾:

right? He said: ﴿Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience about what you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾, meaning: about what you do not know. Ibn 'Abbas said: That was because he was a man who acted upon the unseen.

Musa said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command.﴾ He said: ﴿So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you﴾: until I begin to tell you of it and explain its matter to you. So they set out walking, seeking a ship to board. When they got on the ship, ﴿they boarded the ship﴾. The people of the ship said: "These are thieves," and they ordered them to get out. The owner of the ship said: "They are not thieves, but I see the faces of prophets."

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "They went walking along the shore of the sea. A ship passed by them, and they spoke to its people asking them to carry them. They recognized al-Khidr, and so they carried him without a fare. When they entered the sea, al-Khidr took an axe and broke a plank of the ship until the water entered it. Musa filled it with his garment and said to him: ﴿Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?﴾" [Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/39, with variation.] [86]

The people of Kufa read (liyaghraqa) with an open yaʼ and (ahluha) with a raised lam, making the verb belong to them; this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. ﴿Indeed you have done a thing (shay'an) terrible (imran)﴾, that is, something objectionable. Al-Qutaybi said: wonderful. In the language of the Arabs, al-Imr is a calamity. The rajiz said:

"The rivals have met from me a terrible thing,
a great calamity, a grave, terrible matter" [al-Sihah: 2/581.]

Its root meaning is: everything that is severe and abundant; one says "amara al-qawm" when they multiply and their matter becomes severe.

He said: ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ Musa said: ﴿Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot﴾

[Akhbarana Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq from Hamid ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Sa'd ibn Musa al-Marwarudhi said in Baghdad, and we were informed by Muhammad ibn Abi Najiyya al-Iskandarani from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna from 'Amr ibn Dinar from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] 'Ikrima from Ibn 'Abbas from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The first was from the matter of forgetting, the second was by decree, and had Musa been patient, Allah would have related to us more than He related." [87] [[Tarikh Madinat Dimashq: 61/155, ed. Dar al-Fikr.]]

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: As for him, he did not forget, but it was a form of indirect speech (ma'arid al-kalam). Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is "for what you left of your covenant." ﴿And do not burden me (turhiqni)﴾: hasten me [[Zad al-Masir: 5/120, attributing it to al-Farra'.]]. It was said: do not cover me ([[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 15/354.]]) ﴿with difficulty in my affair﴾: he says, do not constrict my affair and my companionship with you.

﴿So they set out until, when they met a boy﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-Khidr found boys playing, and he took a handsome, bright-faced boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. Ibn 'Abbas said: he had not yet reached puberty.

Al-Dahhak said: He was a boy who did corruption, and his parents were harmed by him; his name was Khashbud. Shu'ayb al-Hayyani said: his name was Hayshur. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: his father's name was Mulas, and his mother's name was Rahmi. Al-Kalbi said: he was a youth who cut the road, took goods, and would take refuge with his parents, who would swear on his behalf; so al-Khidr seized him, threw him down, then pulled his head from his body. Some people said: he kicked him with his foot and killed him. Others said: he struck his head against the wall and killed him.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman from Yahya ibn Qays from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed as a disbeliever [Musnad Ahmad: 5/121]. When he killed him, Musa said to him: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul without its having killed anyone?﴾" [88]

That is: pure. It was said: Muslim. Al-Kisa'i said: al-Zakiya and al-Zakiyya are two dialects, like al-Qasiya and al-Qasiyya. Abu 'Amr said: al-Zakiya is one who has never sinned at all, while al-Zakiyya is one who sinned and then repented. ﴿Without a soul﴾: that is, without his having killed a soul that required retaliation. ﴿Indeed you have done a thing (shay'an) abominable (nukra)﴾: objectionable. Qatada and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Nukr is more severe and greater than al-Imr.

He said: ﴿Did I not say to you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ He said: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this﴾, that is, this time, ﴿then do not keep company with me; you have reached from me an excuse (udhran)﴾ regarding my parting.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Makki ibn 'Abdan from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad: Akhbarana Hamza al-Zayyat from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned anyone and prayed for him, he began with himself. One day he said: "May Allah's mercy be upon us and upon my brother Musa. Had he remained with his companion, he would have seen wonders [al-'ajab] [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; the manuscript has al-a'ajib.]], but he said: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me; you have reached from me an excuse.﴾" [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/392, where it reads al-'ajib instead of al-'ajab.]] [89]

﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning Antioch. Ibn Sirin said: Ayla [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; the manuscript has al-Ayla.]], which is the farthest land of Allah from the sky. ﴿They asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them﴾, that is, to host them as guests. That is because they asked them for food and they did not feed them, and they asked for hospitality and they did not host them.

[Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman from Yahya ibn Qays from Abu Ishaq from] [[Addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿but they refused to entertain them﴾, and he said: "They were a town of miserly people." [90] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/461, no. 4500.]]

Qatada said regarding this verse: the worst of towns is the one that does not host the guest and does not recognize the right of the wayfarer.

They found within it a wall, i.e., in the town, [about to fall]. Wahb said: It was a wall whose height in the sky was one hundred cubits, "about to collapse." This is figurative speech (majaz), because a wall has no will; its meaning is that it came close to and drew near that state, like the words of God Most High: ﴿The heavens are about to burst apart from it﴾ [[Surat Maryam: 90.]]. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*"It almost did, or it intended, to slope toward the ground"* [[Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/290.]]

Some of them said: It returned to its companion, because when this state comes from one's Lord, it is His will, like the words of God Most High: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa﴾ [[Surat al-A'raf: 154.]], whereas it is actually the one who is angry who calms down. And He said: ﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾ [[Surat Muhammad: 21.]], whereas it is the people concerned who resolve. Al-Harithi said:

*"The spear desires the chest of Abu Bara'*
*and turns away from the blood of Bani 'Uqayl"* [[Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/358; Lisan al-'Arab: 3/189, where "yu'dil" appears instead of "yarghab."]]

And 'Uqayl said:

*"Indeed, a time that brings together the union of Sulayma*
*is a time that intends kindness"* [[al-Sihah: 2/661; Jami' al-Bayan li-l-Tabari: 15/358.]]

﴿To collapse﴾, i.e., to fall and crumble. From this comes the word for the falling of stars, which is their falling and departure from their places. Yahya ibn 'Umar recited: (yurid an yanqaad), meaning it is uprooted and split. It is said: the tooth (insaddat al-sinn) split from its root. Some of the Kufans said: infiqad (inqiyad) means a split lengthwise. It is said: the wall, the tooth, and the well split (inqada) when they cracked lengthwise.

﴿And he set it up﴾: he made it straight. Ibn 'Abbas said: he demolished it, then sat down and rebuilt it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he wiped the wall and pushed it with his hand, and it became upright.

Musa said: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken﴾ [a reward for it]. Abu 'Amr recited (latakhadhta), and both are dialectal variants, like your saying (ittaba'a) and (taba'a), and (ittaqa) and (taqa). The poet said:

*"I have taken my saddle beside its stirrup,*
*a sandy place like the hollow of the sand-grouse's nest"* [[al-Sihah: 4/1431.]]

Al-Zajjaj cited in (latakhadhta) the verse of Abu Shammam al-Sabbabi:

*"They took iron from iron as hammers,*
*whose dwellers are spirits and bodies"*

﴿For it﴾, i.e., for its repair and erection, ﴿a wage﴾: a reward and payment. It was also said: hospitality and provision.

Then the Khidr (peace be upon him) said: ﴿This is the parting between me and you.﴾ Lahiq ibn Humayd recited (firaqun) with tanwin. ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not hold patience.﴾ ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾. Ka'b said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were disabled and five of whom worked at sea.

In His words ﴿to poor people﴾ there is evidence that a poor person (miskin), even if he owns something, does not lose the designation of poverty if he has a need for something beyond what he owns, and it is permissible for him to take zakat. [Abu Bakr 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ali al-Hamshadhi informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Razi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Zakariyya al-Maqdisi, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-San'ani, from Ibrahim] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; the adopted copy has instead: "and it was narrated."]] ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: concerning His words, ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who work on the sea﴾ — they were poor while the boat was worth a thousand dinars? He said: Indeed, a traveler is poor even if he has a thousand dinars with him.

﴿So I intended to damage it, and behind them was﴾ — i.e., in front of them and ahead of them, like His words: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [[Surat Ibrahim: 16.]] and ﴿Behind them is a barrier﴾ [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 100.]], meaning in front of them. The poet said:

*"Do the sons of Marwan hope for my hearing and obedience,*
*while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me?"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/390.]]

It was also said: ﴿behind them﴾ means after them, and their return on their journey would be past it, but they did not know of its condition, so God informed the Khidr of its condition. ﴿A king who seizes every boat by force﴾, i.e., every sound boat. He relied on the context to indicate this, and what supports it is what Sufyan related from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited: (wa kana amamahum malikun yakhudhu kulla safinatin salihatin ghasban) ["and in front of them was a king who seized every sound boat by force"]. So he damaged it and made it defective, so that this king would not seize it. His name was Jalanda, and he was an unbeliever. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His name was Manawah ibn Jalanda al-Ardani. Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: his name was Hadad ibn Badad.

﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared﴾ — i.e., we knew. In the codex of Ubayy: (fakhafa rabbuka), meaning he knew, and parallels to this are numerous. Qutrub said: its meaning is "we disliked," as you say: "I separated the two men out of fear that they would fight," though there is no fear in you, only dislike that they should fight. ﴿That he would overwhelm them﴾, i.e., destroy them. It was also said: cover them. Al-Kalbi said: he would burden them with rebellion and disbelief. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: We feared that his love for him would lead them to bring him into his religion.

﴿So we intended that their Lord should replace him with one better than him in purity, ﴾ i.e., righteousness and Islam, ﴿and nearer in kinship﴾. Ruhm is from kinship (rahim) and relationship (qaraba). It was also said: it is from mercy (rahmah). It is said: rahm and ruhm for mercy, like halk and halk, and 'umur and 'umur. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*"And the womb of one who bends did not bend"* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 12/232.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nearer in kinship﴾ means more joined to the womb and more dutiful to his parents. Qatadah said: nearer in good. Ibn Jurayj said: meaning more merciful to them than they were toward the one slain. Al-Farra' said: ﴿and nearer that they would show mercy to him﴾. Al-Kalbi said: God replaced them with a girl, whom a prophet among the prophets married, and she bore him a prophet through whom God, Mighty and Majestic, guided a nation.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Qadi informed us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Falih, from Maymun ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qaddah, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning this verse, who said: "He replaced them with a girl, and she bore seventy prophets." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 6/376.]] [91]

Ibn Jurayj said: He replaced them with a righteous Muslim boy, whereas the one slain was an unbeliever. Likewise in the codex of Ubayy: (As for the boy, he was an unbeliever, and his parents were believers). Qatadah said: his parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved over him when he was killed; had he lived, their destruction would have been in him. So let a person be content with the decree of God, for God's decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he loves.

﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, named Asram and Sarim, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them.﴾ They differed about what that treasure was. Some of them said: it was sheets of knowledge buried beneath it; this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ibn 'Abbas said: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "It was a tablet of gold on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I marvel at one who believes in destiny, how he can grieve; I marvel at one who is certain of provision, how he can toil; I marvel at one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice; I marvel at one who believes in reckoning, how he can be heedless; I marvel at one who knows the world and how it turns its people over, how he can feel at ease in it. There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/38.]]

It has also been reported from the Prophet ﷺ, in some narrations, that this saying was written on that tablet beneath what these verses mention: "O one who is anxious, you are anxious about what does not concern you. If fever seizes you, you will be feverish [....] [[Blank in the manuscript photograph.]] you have risen to a lofty height of knowledge; how can it guard you when the pen has dried?!" [92]

'Ikrimah said: That treasure was wealth.

[Abu Bakr al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Qaydus al-Ta'ra'iqi told us, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Salih al-Thaqafi [[In the Isfahan copy: al-Dimashqi. Marginal note in the manuscript.]], from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Yazid ibn Yusuf al-San'ani, from Yazid ibn Abi Yazid, from] [[Not in the adopted copy.]] Makhul, from [Abu] [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis: 174; the manuscript reads: Umm.]] al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning His words ﴿and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾: "It was gold and silver." [[Zad al-Masir: 5/126.]] [93]

﴿And their father was righteous﴾. His name was Kashih, and he was among the pious. It is mentioned that the two were preserved through the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness of theirs is mentioned. Between them and the father through whom they were preserved there were seven generations. He was a wanderer.

['Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa, from al-Humaydi, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, preserves through a righteous man his child and his child's child, his clan in which he lives, and the houses around him; they remain in God's protection and concealment.

It is related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that whenever he saw his son he would say: "My son, I shall increase my prayer for your sake, hoping that I may be protected through you," and he would recite this verse. [Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Balkhi, from Ahmad ibn al-Layth ibn al-Khalil, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Haytham ibn 'Abd Allah al-Dabi'i told me, from] [[An addition from the Isfahan copy.]] al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: My father told me, from Yahya ibn Isma'il ibn Muslimah ibn Kuhayl, who said: I had a sister older than me who became confused and lost her mind, and became withdrawn. She was in a room at the far end of the roofs, and she remained in that state for some ten-odd years. Despite losing her mind, she was eager for prayer and purity. One night while I was sleeping, the door of my house knocked at midnight. I said: "Who is this?" She said: "Bahha." I said: "My sister?" She said: "Your sister." I said: "Here I am." I got up, opened the door, and she entered; she had not come to the house for more than ten years. I said to her: "O sister, is there good?" She said: "Good. Last night I came in my dream, and it was said: 'Peace be upon you, O Bahha.' I said: 'And upon you peace.' It was said: 'Indeed God has preserved your father Isma'il ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl through your grandfather Salamah, and has preserved you through your father Isma'il. If you wish, I will pray to God for you to remove what is in you; and if you wish, you may be patient and have Paradise. For Abu Bakr and 'Umar have interceded for you with God, Mighty and Majestic, by the love your father and grandfather had for them.'" I said: "If one of the two must be chosen, then patience in what I am in, and Paradise. For God, Mighty and Majestic, is vast in His creation, and nothing is too great for Him; if He wills, He can bring both together for me." She said: "Then it was said to me: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has brought both together for you, and He is pleased with your father and grandfather for their love of Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Arise and come down.'" He said: So God removed what was in her.

﴿So your Lord intended, O Musa, that they should reach their maturity﴾, i.e., reach their full strength and power. It was also said: eighteen years. ﴿And extract their treasure﴾ that was hidden beneath the wall. ﴿And I did it not by my own command﴾, i.e., by my own opinion and of my own accord, but I did it by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not hold patience over﴾. (istaa'a) and (istaṭā'a) have the same meaning.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verses 83–98 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a account of him.﴾ The scholars differed about his prophethood. Some of them said: He was a prophet. Others said: He was a just and righteous king. [Abu Mansur al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yusuf related from [[In the authoritative copy, the word in its place is: narrated.]] Waki' from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Karim, who said: I heard Mujahid say: Four kings ruled the earth: two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.]

The scholars also differed about the reason he was named Dhu al-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned). Some of them said: He was named that because he ruled over the Byzantines (al-Rum) and the Persians. It was said: Because there was something like two horns on his head. It was said: Because he saw in a dream that he had taken hold of the two horns of the sun, and the interpretation of his dream was that he traversed the East and the West. It was said: Because he called his people to monotheism and they struck him on his right horn; then he called them to monotheism and they struck him on his left horn. It was said: Because he had two fine locks of hair, and a lock of hair is called a horn. It was said: Because he was noble on both sides, from a family of nobility through both his father and his mother.

It was said: Because two generations of people passed away during his lifetime while he was still alive. It was said: Because when he fought, he fought with both his hand and his mount. It was said: Because he was given knowledge of the outward and the inward. It was said: Because he entered into both light and darkness.

﴿Indeed, We established him in the land﴾: We made it easy for him in the land, so he possessed it. ﴿And We guided him to its ways﴾; ﴿and We gave him of everything﴾ that people need. It was said: of everything by which kings gain strength in conquering cities and fighting enemies, ﴿a means﴾: knowledge by which he could reach his goal. Al-Hasan said: a means of reaching wherever he wished. It was said: We brought the regions of the earth close to him, just as We subjected the wind to Solomon (peace be upon him).

﴿So he followed﴾: he took the path and travelled. The people of Kufa recited (فَأَتْبَعَ) ... and (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ) with an alif cut (i.e., as a form of the verb with a hamza) and a jazm on the second.

﴿A way﴾ (sababan): Ibn Abbas said: a station. Mujahid said: a path between the East and the West, like the verse ﴿Perhaps I may reach the means, the means to the heavens﴾, meaning the paths.

﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring﴾. The Abadila (the four men named Abdullah): Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, along with al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Ayyub, and the people of Kufa, recited (ḥāmiyatin) with an alif, meaning hot.

This is supported by what [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; in the authoritative copy the word in its place is: what was narrated.]] Ibrahim al-Taymi related from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, where do you think this sets?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It sets in a hot spring." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/249.]] [94]

Abdullah ibn Amr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the sun when it set and said: "In the hot fire of Allah, in the hot fire of Allah. Were it not for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for it, it would have burned whatever is on the earth." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 16/17.]] [95]

The rest recited (ḥami'atin) with a hamza and without an alif, meaning: possessing mud, which is black clay. This is supported by what Sa'd ibn Aws related from Mus'ab ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it to me as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it: ﴿it sets in a muddy spring﴾. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/246.]] Ka'b said: I find it in the Torah: "in a black spring," which agrees with Ibn Abbas. Abu Usamah related from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Hadir or Ibn Hadir, a man from the Azd, say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I was sitting with Mu'awiya when he recited this verse: "and found it setting in a hot spring." I said: We do not recite it except as "muddy." Mu'awiya said to Abdullah ibn Umar: How do you recite it? He said: As you recited it, O Commander of the Faithful. Ibn Abbas said: I said: The Qur'an was revealed in my house!

Mu'awiya sent for Ka'b, and he came. Mu'awiya said: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah, O Ka'b? He said: As for the Arabic, you are more knowledgeable of it; as for the sun, I find it in the Torah setting in water and mud. I said to Ibn Abbas: If I had been with you both, I would have recited a verse by which you would have gained more support for your view: (muddy). Ibn Abbas said: Then what is it? I said: The words of Tubba':

"Dhu al-Qarnayn had been Muslim before me,
a king before whom kings bow down and prostrate.
He reached the East and the West, seeking
the means of a matter from a wise and guiding One.
Then he saw the place of the sun's setting
in a spring of mud and black clay."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/49, where it reads "maghib" instead of "mu'ad."]]

He said: Ibn Abbas said: What is khalab? I said: Mud in their language. He said: And what is tha'ath? I said: Silt. He said: And what is harmad? I said: Black. He called a man or a boy and said: Write down what this man says.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: It has reached me that the sun is in a spring, which throws it out toward the East.

﴿And he found near it a people﴾, meaning people. ﴿We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them﴾: either you kill them if they do not enter Islam; ﴿or you take them with kindness﴾: that is, you pardon and forgive them. It was said: you take them captive, teach them, and show them the right way.

﴿He said: As for one who wrongs﴾, that is, disbelieves, ﴿we will punish him﴾: we will kill him; ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾: a dreadful one. ﴿But as for one who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a good reward﴾. The people of Kufa recited (jazā'an) in the accusative with tanwin, meaning: so for him is the best reward, the accusative being a verbal noun. The rest recited it in the nominative, as an annexation. It has two interpretations. The first is that by "the best" is meant the righteous deeds. The second is that "the best" means Paradise, and the reward is annexed to both, as in His saying: ﴿and the abode of the Hereafter﴾ [[Surah Yusuf: 109.]], where the abode is the Hereafter; and ﴿that is the upright religion﴾ [[Surah al-Bayyinah: 5.]].

﴿And We will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾: We will soften his speech to him and make the matter easy for him. Mujahid said: "ease" means what is good.

﴿Then he followed a means﴾, that is, he took a path and stages. ﴿Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾. Qatadah said: There was no screen between them and the sun.
