When he crossed rivers and seas, he dismantled the boats, then gave each man among them a plank that its load did not weigh down. This was his practice until he reached Hawil, where he did with its people what he had done with the people of Nasik. When he came out of it, he continued on his way through the right-hand region of the earth until he reached a place of worship (*Mansik*) at the rising of the sun. There he did what he had done, and he mustered troops from among them, as he had done with the two peoples before them.

Then he turned back, heading west, until he took the left-hand region of the earth. He intended Tawil, the people opposite Hawil, and the two of them face each other across the whole breadth of the earth. When he reached them, he did with them as he had done with those before them, and he mustered troops from among them.

When he had finished with them, he turned from them to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from among the jinn and mankind, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was partway along the road, on the side near the end of the land of the Turks toward the east, a righteous people from mankind said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there is a creation of God, the Exalted, that has none of the likeness of mankind. They have the likeness of beasts. They eat grass and prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do. They eat [insects] [[From ʿArāʾis al-Majālis. The manuscript reads: fasdah.]] the whole earth, including snakes, beasts, scorpions, and every living thing that God has created. No creation of God grows as they grow in a single generation, and none multiplies as they multiply. If a period passes in which they keep growing and multiplying as you see, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, drive its people out of it, prevail over it, and corrupt it. Not a year has passed since we neighboured them without our expecting that their first will come upon us from between these two mountains. So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you place between us and them a barrier?" He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better. But help me with strength, and I will set between you and them a rampart. Bring me blocks of iron and copper, until I survey their land, learn their ways, and measure the distance between their two mountains."

Then he set out, leading them, until he reached them and came into the middle of their land. He found them all of one size, males and females, the height of each of them about half the height of a medium-built man among us.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: "Some of them are a span tall, and some are excessively tall. They have claws on their fingernails in front of us, and fangs and molars like the molars of beasts of prey. When they eat, their fangs make a sound like the grinding of a camel's cud, or like the chewing of an old mule or a strong horse. They have a down of hair on their bodies that covers them and protects them against heat and cold when these strike. Each of them has two large ears, one with hair and the other with fine down. He wraps himself in one and spreads the other as a bed. He spends summer in one and winter in the other. No male or female among them is without knowing the term of his life and the end of his lifespan. A male among them does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of his loins, and a female does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of her womb. When that time comes, he knows that death is certain. They are provided with *al-sinan* [[So in the manuscript; the source reads: al-tinin.]] in the days of spring, as rain is sought, and immediately they cast out one of them each year, and they eat it for their whole year until the same time next year. Thus it suffices them despite their numbers. They call to one another like pigeons call, they howl like wolves howl, and they mate like beasts mate wherever they meet."

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two cliffs. He measured the distance between them. He was at the far end of the land of the Turks, on the side facing the rising of the sun, and he found that the distance between them was one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh. He made its filling of rock and its mortar of molten copper poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper. He placed between these a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like striped cloth, with the yellowness and redness of copper within the blackness of iron.

When he had finished it and made it firm, he set out intending to go to the community of mankind. While he was travelling, he came upon a righteous people who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a people who were equitable and moderate, who stand upright and judge with justice and show mercy to one another. Their condition was one, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was straight, their hearts were bound together in affection, their conduct was even. Their graves were by the doors of their houses, and their houses had no doors. They had no rulers, no judges, no rich men, no kings, and no nobles. They did not dispute or boast, nor quarrel, nor abuse one another [[That is, one of them abuses another.]], nor kill, nor laugh, nor become angry, and the calamities that afflict people did not afflict them. They were the longest-lived of people, and there was among them no needy or poor man, no coarse or harsh one.

When he saw this condition of theirs, he marvelled and said: "Tell me, O people, your story. I have surveyed all the earth, its land and sea, its east and west, and I have not seen anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are your graves by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did this deliberately, so that we do not forget death, and so that its remembrance does not leave our hearts."

He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no suspected person among us. Among us there is only a trustworthy, entrusted one."

He said: "Then why do you have no ruler?" They said: "We have no need of that."

He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute."

He said: "Then why do you have no rich men among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulating wealth."

He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not boast."

He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or dispute?" They said: "Because of the affection of our hearts and the good state of our relations."

He said: "Then why do you not fight one another?" They said: "Because we have restrained ourselves by our minds [[That is, their intellects.]]."

He said: "Then why is your word one and your way straight?" They said: "Because we do not compete in accumulation, we do not deceive one another, and none of us betrays another."

He said: "Then tell me, how did your hearts become alike and your conduct become upright?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so resentment and envy have been removed from our hearts by this."

He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor man among you?" They said: "Because we divide equally."

He said: "Then why is there no coarse or harsh one among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness."

He said: "Then what has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice."

He said: "Then why do you not laugh?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness."

He said: "Then why do you not grieve or become angry?" They said: "Because since we existed we have prepared ourselves for trials, we have loved them, and we have eagerly sought them."

He said: "Then why do calamities not afflict you as they afflict people?" They said: "Because we rely on none but God, and we do not practise omens or stars."

He said: "And so you found your forefathers doing?" They said: "Yes. We found our forefathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, showing forbearance to those who acted ignorantly towards them, keeping their kinship ties, fulfilling their trusts, guarding the times of their prayers, keeping their covenants, and being truthful in their promises. By this God, mighty and majestic, set their affairs right and preserved them while they were alive. It was indeed due from God that He should make them successors in their descendants."

Qatadah related from Abu Rafi' from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through it every day until, when they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God, mighty and majestic, restores it stronger than it was. When their term is fulfilled and they dig until they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow, God willing.' It returns to them just as it was when they left it. They dig through it and come out upon the people and drink the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and the arrows return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God, mighty and majestic, sends a worm [[In the Isfahan copy: a worm. (Marginal note in the manuscript.)]] upon them in their necks, and they die." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and become sated from their flesh."

Mahmud ibn Qatadah related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say:

'Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out as God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿and they will swarm from every slope﴾ [Qur'an 21:96]. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their fortresses and cities, until the first of them pass by the river, one of the rivers of the earth, [and drink it].'"

Abu al-Haytham said: the Tigris. "They will drink until it becomes dry land. Those who come after them will pass by it and say: 'There was water in this place once.' When they prevail over the people of the earth they say: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them, and only the people of heaven remain.'"

He (ﷺ) said: "One of them will shake his spear and then hurl it toward the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a trial. While they are in that state, God, mighty and majestic, will send upon them worms like the locust's larva, and they will die like locusts die. In the morning the Muslims will hear no sound from them, and they will say: 'Is there any man who will sell himself for us, to go and see what these people have done?' A man from among them will go down, having become certain that he will be killed. He will find them dead, some upon others, and he will call out to his companions: 'Rejoice, for God, mighty and majestic, has spared you their enemy.' Then the Muslims will come out and send their livestock to graze among them, and they will have no pasture except their flesh, and it will swell upon it more than it swells upon any plant that has ever touched it."

Wahb said: "They used to come to the sea and drink its water, and eat its creatures. Then they would eat wood, trees, and whatever people they could seize. They could not reach Mecca, Medina, or Bayt al-Maqdis."

Concerning His saying, ﴿Shall we pay you a tribute?﴾: the people of Kufa read *kharājan* with an *alif*, while the rest read it without *alif*. The two are dialectal variants with one meaning. Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla said: *al-kharj* is what you give voluntarily, and *al-kharāj* is what is obligatory for you to pay. ﴿On condition that you place between us and them a barrier?﴾: a barrier so that they cannot reach us? Dhu al-Qarnayn said to them: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better.﴾ The people of Mecca read *mā makannī* with two nūns and clear pronunciation (*izhār*), while others read it with assimilation (*idghām*). ﴿What my Lord has established me in﴾ means what my Lord has strengthened me to do and empowered me for. ﴿But help me with strength, and I will set between you and them a rampart﴾: a barrier like a wall and a dam.

They said: "And what is that strength?" He said: "Workers and craftsmen who are skilled in building, work, and tools." They said: "And what is that tool?" He said: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, meaning: give me pieces of iron, whose singular is *zubra*. So they brought them to him, and he built, ﴿until when he had made the two cliffs level﴾. Muslim ibn Khalid related from Saʿid ibn Abi Salih, who said: "We have been told that he placed wood between the two mountains, then laid iron over it, then laid wood over the iron. He continued to place wood on iron and iron on wood ﴿until when he had made the two cliffs level﴾." The two cliffs are *al-sadafayn*, read with *ḍamma* and *fatḥa* on the *ṣād* and *dāl*. He ordered fire to be set to it and said: ﴿Blow﴾. Then he began pouring molten copper upon it. That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour upon it molten copper﴾, meaning the molten copper. He said: "The fire began to consume the wood, and copper was poured in place of the wood until the copper bonded to the iron."

﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they pierce it﴾: they could not climb over it from above, nor could they dig through it from below.

Qatadah said: "It was related to us that a man said: 'O Prophet of God, I have seen the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj.' He said: 'Describe it to me.' He said: 'Like striped cloth, with a black stripe and a red stripe.' He said: 'You have indeed seen it.'"

Dhu al-Qarnayn said, when he had finished building it, meaning this barrier: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord﴾, a blessing from my Lord. Therefore he did not say "these." ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾ *Dakkāʾ* means made level and joined to the ground, from the saying "a she-camel that is *dakkāʾ*," meaning level-backed, with no hump. Whoever reads *dakkan* without the long vowel means: crushed on that day. ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verses 83–98 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a account of him.﴾ The scholars differed about his prophethood. Some of them said: He was a prophet. Others said: He was a just and righteous king. [Abu Mansur al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yusuf related from [[In the authoritative copy, the word in its place is: narrated.]] Waki' from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Karim, who said: I heard Mujahid say: Four kings ruled the earth: two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.]

The scholars also differed about the reason he was named Dhu al-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned). Some of them said: He was named that because he ruled over the Byzantines (al-Rum) and the Persians. It was said: Because there was something like two horns on his head. It was said: Because he saw in a dream that he had taken hold of the two horns of the sun, and the interpretation of his dream was that he traversed the East and the West. It was said: Because he called his people to monotheism and they struck him on his right horn; then he called them to monotheism and they struck him on his left horn. It was said: Because he had two fine locks of hair, and a lock of hair is called a horn. It was said: Because he was noble on both sides, from a family of nobility through both his father and his mother.

It was said: Because two generations of people passed away during his lifetime while he was still alive. It was said: Because when he fought, he fought with both his hand and his mount. It was said: Because he was given knowledge of the outward and the inward. It was said: Because he entered into both light and darkness.

﴿Indeed, We established him in the land﴾: We made it easy for him in the land, so he possessed it. ﴿And We guided him to its ways﴾; ﴿and We gave him of everything﴾ that people need. It was said: of everything by which kings gain strength in conquering cities and fighting enemies, ﴿a means﴾: knowledge by which he could reach his goal. Al-Hasan said: a means of reaching wherever he wished. It was said: We brought the regions of the earth close to him, just as We subjected the wind to Solomon (peace be upon him).

﴿So he followed﴾: he took the path and travelled. The people of Kufa recited (فَأَتْبَعَ) ... and (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ) with an alif cut (i.e., as a form of the verb with a hamza) and a jazm on the second.

﴿A way﴾ (sababan): Ibn Abbas said: a station. Mujahid said: a path between the East and the West, like the verse ﴿Perhaps I may reach the means, the means to the heavens﴾, meaning the paths.

﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring﴾. The Abadila (the four men named Abdullah): Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, along with al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Ayyub, and the people of Kufa, recited (ḥāmiyatin) with an alif, meaning hot.

This is supported by what [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; in the authoritative copy the word in its place is: what was narrated.]] Ibrahim al-Taymi related from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, where do you think this sets?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It sets in a hot spring." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/249.]] [94]

Abdullah ibn Amr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the sun when it set and said: "In the hot fire of Allah, in the hot fire of Allah. Were it not for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for it, it would have burned whatever is on the earth." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 16/17.]] [95]

The rest recited (ḥami'atin) with a hamza and without an alif, meaning: possessing mud, which is black clay. This is supported by what Sa'd ibn Aws related from Mus'ab ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it to me as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it: ﴿it sets in a muddy spring﴾. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/246.]] Ka'b said: I find it in the Torah: "in a black spring," which agrees with Ibn Abbas. Abu Usamah related from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Hadir or Ibn Hadir, a man from the Azd, say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I was sitting with Mu'awiya when he recited this verse: "and found it setting in a hot spring." I said: We do not recite it except as "muddy." Mu'awiya said to Abdullah ibn Umar: How do you recite it? He said: As you recited it, O Commander of the Faithful. Ibn Abbas said: I said: The Qur'an was revealed in my house!

Mu'awiya sent for Ka'b, and he came. Mu'awiya said: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah, O Ka'b? He said: As for the Arabic, you are more knowledgeable of it; as for the sun, I find it in the Torah setting in water and mud. I said to Ibn Abbas: If I had been with you both, I would have recited a verse by which you would have gained more support for your view: (muddy). Ibn Abbas said: Then what is it? I said: The words of Tubba':

"Dhu al-Qarnayn had been Muslim before me,
a king before whom kings bow down and prostrate.
He reached the East and the West, seeking
the means of a matter from a wise and guiding One.
Then he saw the place of the sun's setting
in a spring of mud and black clay."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/49, where it reads "maghib" instead of "mu'ad."]]

He said: Ibn Abbas said: What is khalab? I said: Mud in their language. He said: And what is tha'ath? I said: Silt. He said: And what is harmad? I said: Black. He called a man or a boy and said: Write down what this man says.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: It has reached me that the sun is in a spring, which throws it out toward the East.

﴿And he found near it a people﴾, meaning people. ﴿We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them﴾: either you kill them if they do not enter Islam; ﴿or you take them with kindness﴾: that is, you pardon and forgive them. It was said: you take them captive, teach them, and show them the right way.

﴿He said: As for one who wrongs﴾, that is, disbelieves, ﴿we will punish him﴾: we will kill him; ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾: a dreadful one. ﴿But as for one who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a good reward﴾. The people of Kufa recited (jazā'an) in the accusative with tanwin, meaning: so for him is the best reward, the accusative being a verbal noun. The rest recited it in the nominative, as an annexation. It has two interpretations. The first is that by "the best" is meant the righteous deeds. The second is that "the best" means Paradise, and the reward is annexed to both, as in His saying: ﴿and the abode of the Hereafter﴾ [[Surah Yusuf: 109.]], where the abode is the Hereafter; and ﴿that is the upright religion﴾ [[Surah al-Bayyinah: 5.]].

﴿And We will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾: We will soften his speech to him and make the matter easy for him. Mujahid said: "ease" means what is good.

﴿Then he followed a means﴾, that is, he took a path and stages. ﴿Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾. Qatadah said: There was no screen between them and the sun. That was because they lived in a place where no building could stand, and they were in their drink; when the sun moved away from them, they went out to their livelihood and their fields. Al-Hasan said: Their land could not bear building, and when the sun rose over them they dove into the water; when it had risen high, they came out and grazed like cattle.

Ibn Jurayj said: Once an army came to them, and their people said: "The sun will not rise on you while you are here." They said: "We will not leave until the sun rises." They said: "What are these bones?" They said: "These are the corpses of an army on which the sun rose here, and they died." He said: So they fled in terror across the land. Qatadah said: It is said they were the Zanj. Al-Kalbi said: They were Taris, Tawil, and Mansak, naked, barefoot, and blind to the truth. He said: Amr ibn Malik ibn Umayya related to us, saying: I found a man in Samarqand telling people who were gathered around him, and I asked one of those who had heard his talk, and he told me that he had spoken to them about the people over whom the sun rises. He said: I set out until I passed China, then I asked about them, and I was told: Between you and them is a day and night's journey. So I hired a man and travelled the rest of my evening and night until I reached them in the morning. There, one of them was spreading out one ear and wearing the other. He said: My companion was fluent in their language, so he asked them and said: "We have come to see how the sun rises." He said: While we were like that, we heard something like a clattering sound, and I fainted and fell down, and when I came to, they were rubbing me with oil. When the sun rose over the water, it looked like oil on the water, and the edge of the sky looked like a tent. When it had risen, they brought me and my companion into their garments, and when the day had risen, they went out to the sea and began fishing, tossing the fish into the sun where they were cooked.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Thus﴾: the scholars differed about it. Some of them said: meaning as he reached the setting place of the sun, so he also reached its rising place. It was said: ﴿He followed a means﴾ just as he followed a means. It was said: just as he found [the two peoples] [[An illegible word; the apparent reading is what we have put.]] at the setting place of the sun and judged among them, so he found them at the rising place of the sun and judged among them by the same judgment. It was said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, related his story to him, He said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning their matter and their report are as We have told you. Then He began again and said: ﴿And We encompassed what was with him﴾, meaning with him and in his possession of kingdom, armies, and equipment, ﴿with knowledge﴾: [with full knowledge].

﴿Then he followed a means. Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Asim recited (sadday) with a fatha on the sin. The rest recited with a damma. Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, and they are two mountains. Dhu al-Qarnayn set a barrier between them, a separation between Gog and Magog and those beyond them. Ikrimah said: What is the work of human beings is a sadd (with a fatha on the sin), and what is the work of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a sadd (with a damma). Ibn Abbas said: The two barriers are Armenia and Azerbaijan. ﴿He found beside them a people who could scarcely understand a word﴾. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i recited (yufqihūn) with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the qaf, meaning "they make others understand." The rest recited (yafqahūn) with a fatha on the ya and the qaf, meaning they understand and comprehend speech.

﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn﴾. It was said: Other people spoke to him on their behalf, through an interpreter. The explanation of this is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "They could scarcely understand a word. Those who were beyond them said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn." It was said: The meaning is: they could scarcely understand good from evil, or misguidance from guidance.

﴿Indeed, Gog and Magog﴾: Asim and al-A'raj recited them with a hamza; the rest without a hamza. They are two dialects. They said: The word is derived from (ajij al-nar), which is its flame and sparks, and they were compared to it in their number and their strength. Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: They are from the offspring of Japheth, son of Noah. Al-Dahhak said: They are a generation of the Turks. Ka'b said: They are a unique line of the children of Adam without Eve. That is because Adam (peace be upon him) took a midday nap one day, had a wet dream, and his semen mixed with the dust. When he woke, he regretted the water that had come out of him. So Allah, Exalted, created Gog and Magog from that water, and they are connected to us through the father but not through the mother.

And His saying: ﴿spreading corruption in the land﴾. Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Their corruption in the land was that they used to eat people. Al-Kalbi said: They would go out to their land in the spring and leave nothing green without eating it, and nothing dry without carrying it off into their land. They caused great harm and killing. It was said: The meaning is that they will spread corruption in the land when they come out.

[Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan related to us from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Nasawi, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from [[An addition from another copy; in the authoritative copy the word in its place is: narrated.]] al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about Gog and Magog, and he said: "Gog is a nation and Magog is a nation. Each nation has four hundred thousand nations. No man of them dies until he sees a thousand males from his own loins, all of them carrying weapons." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us." He said: "They are three types: one type is like the arz (a tree), and it was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the arz? He said: A tree in Syria whose height is one hundred and twenty cubits into the sky. Another type is as wide as it is long, one hundred and twenty cubits. Another type spreads out one ear and wraps itself in the other. They do not pass by an elephant, a wild beast, or a pig without eating it, and whoever of them dies, they eat him. Their vanguard is in Syria and their rear guard is in Khurasan, and they drink the rivers of the East and the Lake of Tiberias."] [96] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/6, with slight variation.]]

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the Byzantines, the son of an old woman from among their old women who had no child but him. His name was Alexander. When he reached maturity, and he was a righteous servant, Allah, Exalted, said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, I am sending you to the nations of the earth. They are nations with different tongues, and they are all the people of the earth. Among them are two nations, one spanning the length of the whole earth and one spanning its breadth. Among the nations in the middle of the earth are the jinn, humankind, Gog and Magog. As for the two nations that span the length of the earth, one nation is at the setting place of the sun, called Nasik, and the other is at its rising place, called Mansak. As for the two nations spanning the breadth of the earth, one nation is at the right side of the earth, called Hawil, and the other is at the left side of the earth, called Tawil." [[In the source, the word is "they," not "it."]] [[In the source: "[And they are of kinds: two nations spanning the whole length of the earth] instead of [and they are all the people of the earth]."]] When Allah, Exalted, said this to him, Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "O my God, You have appointed me to a great matter whose extent none but You can measure. Tell me about these nations to which You have sent me: with what strength can I overcome their greatest ones? With what host and what cunning can I outnumber them? With what patience can I console them? With what tongue can I speak with them? How can I come to understand their languages? With what hearing can I hear their words? With what sight can I scrutinize them? With what proof can I dispute with them? With what intellect can I understand them? With what wisdom can I manage their affairs? With what justice can I be just among them? With what forbearance can I endure them? With what knowledge can I distinguish between them? With what learning can I perfect their affairs? With what hand can I seize them? With what foot can I tread upon them? With what capacity can I count them? With what army can I fight them? With what gentleness can I win them over? O my God, I have none of what You have mentioned that can stand with them, overcome them, or bear them. You are the Compassionate, the Merciful, who does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, nor lay on it except what it can bear, nor cause it hardship, but You are merciful to it." Allah, Exalted, said: "I will give you the strength to bear what I have laid upon you. I will open your breast so that you will hear everything; I will open your understanding so that you will understand everything; I will loosen your tongue so that you will speak everything; I will open your hearing so that you will be aware of everything; I will extend your sight so that you will scrutinize everything; I will count for you so that nothing escapes you; I will strengthen your arm so that nothing frightens you; I will strengthen your side so that nothing overcomes you; I will strengthen your heart so that nothing alarms you; I will guard you so that nothing is hidden from you; I will extend for you from before you so that you will prevail over everything; I will strengthen your stride so that you will crush everything; I will clothe you with awe so that nothing terrifies you; and I will subject to you light and darkness, making them two of My hosts: light will guide you from before you, and darkness will shield you from behind you." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/51; and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: 218, with variation and addition here.]] [97]

When he was told this, he set out to head toward the nations at the setting place of the sun. When he reached them, he found a multitude and a number that none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, could count, and a strength and might that none but Allah could overcome, and differing tongues and scattered desires. When he saw this, he overcame them with darkness. He set three armies of it around them and encircled them from every direction until he had gathered them in one place. Then he seized them with light and called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to worship Him. ﴿Some of them believed﴾...

﴿And some of them turned away from him﴾. He turned to those who had turned their backs on him and brought darkness upon them. It entered their mouths, ears, noses, and bellies, and entered their houses and dwellings, and covered them from above, below, and every side. They surged in it and were bewildered. When they feared they would perish in it, they cried out to him with one voice, and he removed it from them and took them by force. So they entered his call, and he drafted great nations from the people of the West and made them one army.

Then he set out with them, leading them, while darkness drove them and guarded them from behind, and light was before them, leading them and guiding him. He went along the right side of the earth, intending the nation at the right side of the earth called Hawil. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, subjected to him his hand, his heart, his mind, his opinion, and his sight, so he never erred when he acted.

Then he set off leading those peoples, and they followed him. Whenever he reached a sea or a narrow pass, he built boats from small planks, like mules in size. He assembled them within an hour, then carried on them all of those with him, both peoples and troops. When he crossed rivers and seas, he dismantled the boats, then gave each man among them a plank that its load did not weigh down. This was his practice until he reached Hawil, where he did with its people what he had done with the people of Nasik. When he came out of it, he continued on his way through the right-hand region of the earth until he reached a place of worship (*Mansik*) at the rising of the sun. There he did what he had done, and he mustered troops from among them, as he had done with the two peoples before them.

Then he turned back, heading west, until he took the left-hand region of the earth. He intended Tawil, the people opposite Hawil, and the two of them face each other across the whole breadth of the earth. When he reached them, he did with them as he had done with those before them, and he mustered troops from among them.

When he had finished with them, he turned from them to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from among the jinn and mankind, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was partway along the road, on the side near the end of the land of the Turks toward the east, a righteous people from mankind said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there is a creation of God, the Exalted, that has none of the likeness of mankind. They have the likeness of beasts. They eat grass and prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do. They eat [insects] [[From ʿArāʾis al-Majālis. The manuscript reads: fasdah.]] the whole earth, including snakes, beasts, scorpions, and every living thing that God has created. No creation of God grows as they grow in a single generation, and none multiplies as they multiply. If a period passes in which they keep growing and multiplying as you see, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, drive its people out of it, prevail over it, and corrupt it. Not a year has passed since we neighboured them without our expecting that their first will come upon us from between these two mountains. So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you place between us and them a barrier?" He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better. But help me with strength, and I will set between you and them a rampart. Bring me blocks of iron and copper, until I survey their land, learn their ways, and measure the distance between their two mountains."

Then he set out, leading them, until he reached them and came into the middle of their land. He found them all of one size, males and females, the height of each of them about half the height of a medium-built man among us.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: "Some of them are a span tall, and some are excessively tall. They have claws on their fingernails in front of us, and fangs and molars like the molars of beasts of prey. When they eat, their fangs make a sound like the grinding of a camel's cud, or like the chewing of an old mule or a strong horse. They have a down of hair on their bodies that covers them and protects them against heat and cold when these strike. Each of them has two large ears, one with hair and the other with fine down. He wraps himself in one and spreads the other as a bed. He spends summer in one and winter in the other. No male or female among them is without knowing the term of his life and the end of his lifespan. A male among them does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of his loins, and a female does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of her womb. When that time comes, he knows that death is certain. They are provided with *al-sinan* [[So in the manuscript; the source reads: al-tinin.]] in the days of spring, as rain is sought, and immediately they cast out one of them each year, and they eat it for their whole year until the same time next year. Thus it suffices them despite their numbers. They call to one another like pigeons call, they howl like wolves howl, and they mate like beasts mate wherever they meet."

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two cliffs. He measured the distance between them. He was at the far end of the land of the Turks, on the side facing the rising of the sun, and he found that the distance between them was one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh. He made its filling of rock and its mortar of molten copper poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper. He placed between these a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like striped cloth, with the yellowness and redness of copper within the blackness of iron.

When he had finished it and made it firm, he set out intending to go to the community of mankind. While he was travelling, he came upon a righteous people who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a people who were equitable and moderate, who stand upright and judge with justice and show mercy to one another. Their condition was one, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was straight, their hearts were bound together in affection, their conduct was even. Their graves were by the doors of their houses, and their houses had no doors. They had no rulers, no judges, no rich men, no kings, and no nobles. They did not dispute or boast, nor quarrel, nor abuse one another [[That is, one of them abuses another.]], nor kill, nor laugh, nor become angry, and the calamities that afflict people did not afflict them. They were the longest-lived of people, and there was among them no needy or poor man, no coarse or harsh one.

When he saw this condition of theirs, he marvelled and said: "Tell me, O people, your story. I have surveyed all the earth, its land and sea, its east and west, and I have not seen anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are your graves by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did this deliberately, so that we do not forget death, and so that its remembrance does not leave our hearts."

He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no suspected person among us. Among us there is only a trustworthy, entrusted one."

He said: "Then why do you have no ruler?" They said: "We have no need of that."

He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute."

He said: "Then why do you have no rich men among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulating wealth."

He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not boast."

He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or dispute?" They said: "Because of the affection of our hearts and the good state of our relations."

He said: "Then why do you not fight one another?" They said: "Because we have restrained ourselves by our minds [[That is, their intellects.]]."

He said: "Then why is your word one and your way straight?" They said: "Because we do not compete in accumulation, we do not deceive one another, and none of us betrays another."

He said: "Then tell me, how did your hearts become alike and your conduct become upright?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so resentment and envy have been removed from our hearts by this."

He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor man among you?" They said: "Because we divide equally."

He said: "Then why is there no coarse or harsh one among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness."

He said: "Then what has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice."

He said: "Then why do you not laugh?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness."

He said: "Then why do you not grieve or become angry?" They said: "Because since we existed we have prepared ourselves for trials, we have loved them, and we have eagerly sought them."

He said: "Then why do calamities not afflict you as they afflict people?" They said: "Because we rely on none but God, and we do not practise omens or stars."

He said: "And so you found your forefathers doing?" They said: "Yes. We found our forefathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, showing forbearance to those who acted ignorantly towards them, keeping their kinship ties, fulfilling their trusts, guarding the times of their prayers, keeping their covenants, and being truthful in their promises. By this God, mighty and majestic, set their affairs right and preserved them while they were alive. It was indeed due from God that He should make them successors in their descendants."

Qatadah related from Abu Rafi' from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through it every day until, when they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God, mighty and majestic, restores it stronger than it was. When their term is fulfilled and they dig until they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow, God willing.' It returns to them just as it was when they left it. They dig through it and come out upon the people and drink the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and the arrows return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God, mighty and majestic, sends a worm [[In the Isfahan copy: a worm. (Marginal note in the manuscript.)]] upon them in their necks, and they die." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and become sated from their flesh."

Mahmud ibn Qatadah related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say:

'Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out as God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿and they will swarm from every slope﴾ [Qur'an 21:96]. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their fortresses and cities, until the first of them pass by the river, one of the rivers of the earth, [and drink it].'"

Abu al-Haytham said: the Tigris. "They will drink until it becomes dry land. Those who come after them will pass by it and say: 'There was water in this place once.' When they prevail over the people of the earth they say: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them, and only the people of heaven remain.'"

He (ﷺ) said: "One of them will shake his spear and then hurl it toward the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a trial. While they are in that state, God, mighty and majestic, will send upon them worms like the locust's larva, and they will die like locusts die. In the morning the Muslims will hear no sound from them, and they will say: 'Is there any man who will sell himself for us, to go and see what these people have done?' A man from among them will go down, having become certain that he will be killed. He will find them dead, some upon others, and he will call out to his companions: 'Rejoice, for God, mighty and majestic, has spared you their enemy.' Then the Muslims will come out and send their livestock to graze among them, and they will have no pasture except their flesh, and it will swell upon it more than it swells upon any plant that has ever touched it."

Wahb said: "They used to come to the sea and drink its water, and eat its creatures. Then they would eat wood, trees, and whatever people they could seize. They could not reach Mecca, Medina, or Bayt al-Maqdis."

Concerning His saying, ﴿Shall we pay you a tribute?﴾: the people of Kufa read *kharājan* with an *alif*, while the rest read it without *alif*. The two are dialectal variants with one meaning. Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla said: *al-kharj* is what you give voluntarily, and *al-kharāj* is what is obligatory for you to pay. ﴿On condition that you place between us and them a barrier?﴾: a barrier so that they cannot reach us? Dhu al-Qarnayn said to them: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better.﴾ The people of Mecca read *mā makannī* with two nūns and clear pronunciation (*izhār*), while others read it with assimilation (*idghām*). ﴿What my Lord has established me in﴾ means what my Lord has strengthened me to do and empowered me for. ﴿But help me with strength, and I will set between you and them a rampart﴾: a barrier like a wall and a dam.

They said: "And what is that strength?" He said: "Workers and craftsmen who are skilled in building, work, and tools." They said: "And what is that tool?" He said: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, meaning: give me pieces of iron, whose singular is *zubra*. So they brought them to him, and he built, ﴿until when he had made the two cliffs level﴾. Muslim ibn Khalid related from Saʿid ibn Abi Salih, who said: "We have been told that he placed wood between the two mountains, then laid iron over it, then laid wood over the iron. He continued to place wood on iron and iron on wood ﴿until when he had made the two cliffs level﴾." The two cliffs are *al-sadafayn*, read with *ḍamma* and *fatḥa* on the *ṣād* and *dāl*. He ordered fire to be set to it and said: ﴿Blow﴾. Then he began pouring molten copper upon it. That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour upon it molten copper﴾, meaning the molten copper. He said: "The fire began to consume the wood, and copper was poured in place of the wood until the copper bonded to the iron."

﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they pierce it﴾: they could not climb over it from above, nor could they dig through it from below.

Qatadah said: "It was related to us that a man said: 'O Prophet of God, I have seen the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj.' He said: 'Describe it to me.' He said: 'Like striped cloth, with a black stripe and a red stripe.' He said: 'You have indeed seen it.'"

Dhu al-Qarnayn said, when he had finished building it, meaning this barrier: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord﴾, a blessing from my Lord. Therefore he did not say "these." ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾ *Dakkāʾ* means made level and joined to the ground, from the saying "a she-camel that is *dakkāʾ*," meaning level-backed, with no hump. Whoever reads *dakkan* without the long vowel means: crushed on that day. ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 18, verses 83–98 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a account of him.﴾ The scholars differed about his prophethood. Some of them said: He was a prophet. Others said: He was a just and righteous king. [Abu Mansur al-Hamshadhi informed us: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yusuf related from [[In the authoritative copy, the word in its place is: narrated.]] Waki' from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Karim, who said: I heard Mujahid say: Four kings ruled the earth: two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.]

The scholars also differed about the reason he was named Dhu al-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned). Some of them said: He was named that because he ruled over the Byzantines (al-Rum) and the Persians. It was said: Because there was something like two horns on his head. It was said: Because he saw in a dream that he had taken hold of the two horns of the sun, and the interpretation of his dream was that he traversed the East and the West. It was said: Because he called his people to monotheism and they struck him on his right horn; then he called them to monotheism and they struck him on his left horn. It was said: Because he had two fine locks of hair, and a lock of hair is called a horn. It was said: Because he was noble on both sides, from a family of nobility through both his father and his mother.

It was said: Because two generations of people passed away during his lifetime while he was still alive. It was said: Because when he fought, he fought with both his hand and his mount. It was said: Because he was given knowledge of the outward and the inward. It was said: Because he entered into both light and darkness.

﴿Indeed, We established him in the land﴾: We made it easy for him in the land, so he possessed it. ﴿And We guided him to its ways﴾; ﴿and We gave him of everything﴾ that people need. It was said: of everything by which kings gain strength in conquering cities and fighting enemies, ﴿a means﴾: knowledge by which he could reach his goal. Al-Hasan said: a means of reaching wherever he wished. It was said: We brought the regions of the earth close to him, just as We subjected the wind to Solomon (peace be upon him).

﴿So he followed﴾: he took the path and travelled. The people of Kufa recited (فَأَتْبَعَ) ... and (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ) with an alif cut (i.e., as a form of the verb with a hamza) and a jazm on the second.

﴿A way﴾ (sababan): Ibn Abbas said: a station. Mujahid said: a path between the East and the West, like the verse ﴿Perhaps I may reach the means, the means to the heavens﴾, meaning the paths.

﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring﴾. The Abadila (the four men named Abdullah): Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, along with al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Ayyub, and the people of Kufa, recited (ḥāmiyatin) with an alif, meaning hot.

This is supported by what [[An addition from the Isfahan copy; in the authoritative copy the word in its place is: what was narrated.]] Ibrahim al-Taymi related from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, where do you think this sets?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It sets in a hot spring." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/249.]] [94]

Abdullah ibn Amr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the sun when it set and said: "In the hot fire of Allah, in the hot fire of Allah. Were it not for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained for it, it would have burned whatever is on the earth." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 16/17.]] [95]

The rest recited (ḥami'atin) with a hamza and without an alif, meaning: possessing mud, which is black clay. This is supported by what Sa'd ibn Aws related from Mus'ab ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it to me as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it: ﴿it sets in a muddy spring﴾. [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/246.]] Ka'b said: I find it in the Torah: "in a black spring," which agrees with Ibn Abbas. Abu Usamah related from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Hadir or Ibn Hadir, a man from the Azd, say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I was sitting with Mu'awiya when he recited this verse: "and found it setting in a hot spring." I said: We do not recite it except as "muddy." Mu'awiya said to Abdullah ibn Umar: How do you recite it? He said: As you recited it, O Commander of the Faithful. Ibn Abbas said: I said: The Qur'an was revealed in my house!

Mu'awiya sent for Ka'b, and he came. Mu'awiya said: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah, O Ka'b? He said: As for the Arabic, you are more knowledgeable of it; as for the sun, I find it in the Torah setting in water and mud. I said to Ibn Abbas: If I had been with you both, I would have recited a verse by which you would have gained more support for your view: (muddy). Ibn Abbas said: Then what is it? I said: The words of Tubba':

"Dhu al-Qarnayn had been Muslim before me,
a king before whom kings bow down and prostrate.
He reached the East and the West, seeking
the means of a matter from a wise and guiding One.
Then he saw the place of the sun's setting
in a spring of mud and black clay."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/49, where it reads "maghib" instead of "mu'ad."]]

He said: Ibn Abbas said: What is khalab? I said: Mud in their language. He said: And what is tha'ath? I said: Silt. He said: And what is harmad? I said: Black. He called a man or a boy and said: Write down what this man says.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: It has reached me that the sun is in a spring, which throws it out toward the East.

﴿And he found near it a people﴾, meaning people. ﴿We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them﴾: either you kill them if they do not enter Islam; ﴿or you take them with kindness﴾: that is, you pardon and forgive them. It was said: you take them captive, teach them, and show them the right way.

﴿He said: As for one who wrongs﴾, that is, disbelieves, ﴿we will punish him﴾: we will kill him; ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾: a dreadful one. ﴿But as for one who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a good reward﴾. The people of Kufa recited (jazā'an) in the accusative with tanwin, meaning: so for him is the best reward, the accusative being a verbal noun. The rest recited it in the nominative, as an annexation. It has two interpretations. The first is that by "the best" is meant the righteous deeds. The second is that "the best" means Paradise, and the reward is annexed to both, as in His saying: ﴿and the abode of the Hereafter﴾ [[Surah Yusuf: 109.]], where the abode is the Hereafter; and ﴿that is the upright religion﴾ [[Surah al-Bayyinah: 5.]].

﴿And We will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾: We will soften his speech to him and make the matter easy for him. Mujahid said: "ease" means what is good.

﴿Then he followed a means﴾, that is, he took a path and stages. ﴿Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾. Qatadah said: There was no screen between them and the sun. That was because they lived in a place where no building could stand, and they were in their drink; when the sun moved away from them, they went out to their livelihood and their fields. Al-Hasan said: Their land could not bear building, and when the sun rose over them they dove into the water; when it had risen high, they came out and grazed like cattle.

Ibn Jurayj said: Once an army came to them, and their people said: "The sun will not rise on you while you are here." They said: "We will not leave until the sun rises." They said: "What are these bones?" They said: "These are the corpses of an army on which the sun rose here, and they died." He said: So they fled in terror across the land. Qatadah said: It is said they were the Zanj. Al-Kalbi said: They were Taris, Tawil, and Mansak, naked, barefoot, and blind to the truth. He said: Amr ibn Malik ibn Umayya related to us, saying: I found a man in Samarqand telling people who were gathered around him, and I asked one of those who had heard his talk, and he told me that he had spoken to them about the people over whom the sun rises. He said: I set out until I passed China, then I asked about them, and I was told: Between you and them is a day and night's journey. So I hired a man and travelled the rest of my evening and night until I reached them in the morning. There, one of them was spreading out one ear and wearing the other. He said: My companion was fluent in their language, so he asked them and said: "We have come to see how the sun rises." He said: While we were like that, we heard something like a clattering sound, and I fainted and fell down, and when I came to, they were rubbing me with oil. When the sun rose over the water, it looked like oil on the water, and the edge of the sky looked like a tent. When it had risen, they brought me and my companion into their garments, and when the day had risen, they went out to the sea and began fishing, tossing the fish into the sun where they were cooked.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Thus﴾: the scholars differed about it. Some of them said: meaning as he reached the setting place of the sun, so he also reached its rising place. It was said: ﴿He followed a means﴾ just as he followed a means. It was said: just as he found [the two peoples] [[An illegible word; the apparent reading is what we have put.]] at the setting place of the sun and judged among them, so he found them at the rising place of the sun and judged among them by the same judgment. It was said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, related his story to him, He said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning their matter and their report are as We have told you. Then He began again and said: ﴿And We encompassed what was with him﴾, meaning with him and in his possession of kingdom, armies, and equipment, ﴿with knowledge﴾: [with full knowledge].

﴿Then he followed a means. Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Asim recited (sadday) with a fatha on the sin. The rest recited with a damma. Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, and they are two mountains. Dhu al-Qarnayn set a barrier between them, a separation between Gog and Magog and those beyond them. Ikrimah said: What is the work of human beings is a sadd (with a fatha on the sin), and what is the work of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a sadd (with a damma). Ibn Abbas said: The two barriers are Armenia and Azerbaijan. ﴿He found beside them a people who could scarcely understand a word﴾. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i recited (yufqihūn) with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the qaf, meaning "they make others understand." The rest recited (yafqahūn) with a fatha on the ya and the qaf, meaning they understand and comprehend speech.

﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn﴾. It was said: Other people spoke to him on their behalf, through an interpreter. The explanation of this is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "They could scarcely understand a word. Those who were beyond them said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn." It was said: The meaning is: they could scarcely understand good from evil, or misguidance from guidance.

﴿Indeed, Gog and Magog﴾: Asim and al-A'raj recited them with a hamza; the rest without a hamza. They are two dialects. They said: The word is derived from (ajij al-nar), which is its flame and sparks, and they were compared to it in their number and their strength. Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: They are from the offspring of Japheth, son of Noah. Al-Dahhak said: They are a generation of the Turks. Ka'b said: They are a unique line of the children of Adam without Eve. That is because Adam (peace be upon him) took a midday nap one day, had a wet dream, and his semen mixed with the dust. When he woke, he regretted the water that had come out of him. So Allah, Exalted, created Gog and Magog from that water, and they are connected to us through the father but not through the mother.

And His saying: ﴿spreading corruption in the land﴾. Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Their corruption in the land was that they used to eat people. Al-Kalbi said: They would go out to their land in the spring and leave nothing green without eating it, and nothing dry without carrying it off into their land. They caused great harm and killing. It was said: The meaning is that they will spread corruption in the land when they come out.

[Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan related to us from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Nasawi, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from [[An addition from another copy; in the authoritative copy the word in its place is: narrated.]] al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about Gog and Magog, and he said: "Gog is a nation and Magog is a nation. Each nation has four hundred thousand nations. No man of them dies until he sees a thousand males from his own loins, all of them carrying weapons." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us." He said: "They are three types: one type is like the arz (a tree), and it was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the arz? He said: A tree in Syria whose height is one hundred and twenty cubits into the sky. Another type is as wide as it is long, one hundred and twenty cubits. Another type spreads out one ear and wraps itself in the other. They do not pass by an elephant, a wild beast, or a pig without eating it, and whoever of them dies, they eat him. Their vanguard is in Syria and their rear guard is in Khurasan, and they drink the rivers of the East and the Lake of Tiberias."] [96] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/6, with slight variation.]]

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the Byzantines, the son of an old woman from among their old women who had no child but him. His name was Alexander. When he reached maturity, and he was a righteous servant, Allah, Exalted, said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, I am sending you to the nations of the earth. They are nations with different tongues, and they are all the people of the earth. Among them are two nations, one spanning the length of the whole earth and one spanning its breadth. Among the nations in the middle of the earth are the jinn, humankind, Gog and Magog. As for the two nations that span the length of the earth, one nation is at the setting place of the sun, called Nasik, and the other is at its rising place, called Mansak. As for the two nations spanning the breadth of the earth, one nation is at the right side of the earth, called Hawil, and the other is at the left side of the earth, called Tawil." [[In the source, the word is "they," not "it."]] [[In the source: "[And they are of kinds: two nations spanning the whole length of the earth] instead of [and they are all the people of the earth]."]] When Allah, Exalted, said this to him, Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "O my God, You have appointed me to a great matter whose extent none but You can measure. Tell me about these nations to which You have sent me: with what strength can I overcome their greatest ones? With what host and what cunning can I outnumber them? With what patience can I console them? With what tongue can I speak with them? How can I come to understand their languages? With what hearing can I hear their words? With what sight can I scrutinize them? With what proof can I dispute with them? With what intellect can I understand them? With what wisdom can I manage their affairs? With what justice can I be just among them? With what forbearance can I endure them? With what knowledge can I distinguish between them? With what learning can I perfect their affairs? With what hand can I seize them? With what foot can I tread upon them? With what capacity can I count them? With what army can I fight them? With what gentleness can I win them over? O my God, I have none of what You have mentioned that can stand with them, overcome them, or bear them. You are the Compassionate, the Merciful, who does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, nor lay on it except what it can bear, nor cause it hardship, but You are merciful to it." Allah, Exalted, said: "I will give you the strength to bear what I have laid upon you. I will open your breast so that you will hear everything; I will open your understanding so that you will understand everything; I will loosen your tongue so that you will speak everything; I will open your hearing so that you will be aware of everything; I will extend your sight so that you will scrutinize everything; I will count for you so that nothing escapes you; I will strengthen your arm so that nothing frightens you; I will strengthen your side so that nothing overcomes you; I will strengthen your heart so that nothing alarms you; I will guard you so that nothing is hidden from you; I will extend for you from before you so that you will prevail over everything; I will strengthen your stride so that you will crush everything; I will clothe you with awe so that nothing terrifies you; and I will subject to you light and darkness, making them two of My hosts: light will guide you from before you, and darkness will shield you from behind you." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/51; and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: 218, with variation and addition here.]] [97]

When he was told this, he set out to head toward the nations at the setting place of the sun. When he reached them, he found a multitude and a number that none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, could count, and a strength and might that none but Allah could overcome, and differing tongues and scattered desires. When he saw this, he overcame them with darkness. He set three armies of it around them and encircled them from every direction until he had gathered them in one place. Then he seized them with light and called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to worship Him. ﴿Some of them believed﴾...

﴿And some of them turned away from him﴾. He turned to those who had turned their backs on him and brought darkness upon them. It entered their mouths, ears, noses, and bellies, and entered their houses and dwellings, and covered them from above, below, and every side. They surged in it and were bewildered. When they feared they would perish in it, they cried out to him with one voice, and he removed it from them and took them by force. So they entered his call, and he drafted great nations from the people of the West and made them one army.

Then he set out with them, leading them, while darkness drove them and guarded them from behind, and light was before them, leading them and guiding him. He went along the right side of the earth, intending the nation at the right side of the earth called Hawil. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, subjected to him his hand, his heart, his mind, his opinion, and his sight, so he never erred when he acted.

Then he set off leading those peoples, and they followed him. Whenever he reached a sea or a narrow pass, he built boats from small planks, like mules in size. He assembled them within an hour, then carried on them all of those with him, both peoples and troops. When he crossed rivers and seas, he dismantled the boats, then gave each man among them a plank that its load did not weigh down. This was his practice until he reached Hawil, where he did with its people what he had done with the people of Nasik. When he came out of it, he continued on his way through the right-hand region of the earth until he reached a place of worship (*Mansik*) at the rising of the sun. There he did what he had done, and he mustered troops from among them, as he had done with the two peoples before them.

Then he turned back, heading west, until he took the left-hand region of the earth. He intended Tawil, the people opposite Hawil, and the two of them face each other across the whole breadth of the earth. When he reached them, he did with them as he had done with those before them, and he mustered troops from among them.

When he had finished with them, he turned from them to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from among the jinn and mankind, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was partway along the road, on the side near the end of the land of the Turks toward the east, a righteous people from mankind said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there is a creation of God, the Exalted, that has none of the likeness of mankind. They have the likeness of beasts. They eat grass and prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do. They eat [insects] [[From ʿArāʾis al-Majālis. The manuscript reads: fasdah.]] the whole earth, including snakes, beasts, scorpions, and every living thing that God has created. No creation of God grows as they grow in a single generation, and none multiplies as they multiply. If a period passes in which they keep growing and multiplying as you see, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, drive its people out of it, prevail over it, and corrupt it. Not a year has passed since we neighboured them without our expecting that their first will come upon us from between these two mountains. So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you place between us and them a barrier?" He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better. But help me with strength, and I will set between you and them a rampart. Bring me blocks of iron and copper, until I survey their land, learn their ways, and measure the distance between their two mountains."

Then he set out, leading them, until he reached them and came into the middle of their land. He found them all of one size, males and females, the height of each of them about half the height of a medium-built man among us.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: "Some of them are a span tall, and some are excessively tall. They have claws on their fingernails in front of us, and fangs and molars like the molars of beasts of prey. When they eat, their fangs make a sound like the grinding of a camel's cud, or like the chewing of an old mule or a strong horse. They have a down of hair on their bodies that covers them and protects them against heat and cold when these strike. Each of them has two large ears, one with hair and the other with fine down. He wraps himself in one and spreads the other as a bed. He spends summer in one and winter in the other. No male or female among them is without knowing the term of his life and the end of his lifespan. A male among them does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of his loins, and a female does not die until a thousand offspring have come out of her womb. When that time comes, he knows that death is certain. They are provided with *al-sinan* [[So in the manuscript; the source reads: al-tinin.]] in the days of spring, as rain is sought, and immediately they cast out one of them each year, and they eat it for their whole year until the same time next year. Thus it suffices them despite their numbers. They call to one another like pigeons call, they howl like wolves howl, and they mate like beasts mate wherever they meet."

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two cliffs. He measured the distance between them. He was at the far end of the land of the Turks, on the side facing the rising of the sun, and he found that the distance between them was one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh. He made its filling of rock and its mortar of molten copper poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper. He placed between these a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like striped cloth, with the yellowness and redness of copper within the blackness of iron.

When he had finished it and made it firm, he set out intending to go to the community of mankind. While he was travelling, he came upon a righteous people who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a people who were equitable and moderate, who stand upright and judge with justice and show mercy to one another. Their condition was one, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was straight, their hearts were bound together in affection, their conduct was even. Their graves were by the doors of their houses, and their houses had no doors. They had no rulers, no judges, no rich men, no kings, and no nobles. They did not dispute or boast, nor quarrel, nor abuse one another [[That is, one of them abuses another.]], nor kill, nor laugh, nor become angry, and the calamities that afflict people did not afflict them. They were the longest-lived of people, and there was among them no needy or poor man, no coarse or harsh one.

When he saw this condition of theirs, he marvelled and said: "Tell me, O people, your story. I have surveyed all the earth, its land and sea, its east and west, and I have not seen anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are your graves by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did this deliberately, so that we do not forget death, and so that its remembrance does not leave our hearts."

He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no suspected person among us. Among us there is only a trustworthy, entrusted one."

He said: "Then why do you have no ruler?" They said: "We have no need of that."

He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute."

He said: "Then why do you have no rich men among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulating wealth."

He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not boast."

He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or dispute?" They said: "Because of the affection of our hearts and the good state of our relations."

He said: "Then why do you not fight one another?" They said: "Because we have restrained ourselves by our minds [[That is, their intellects.]]."

He said: "Then why is your word one and your way straight?" They said: "Because we do not compete in accumulation, we do not deceive one another, and none of us betrays another."

He said: "Then tell me, how did your hearts become alike and your conduct become upright?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so resentment and envy have been removed from our hearts by this."

He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor man among you?" They said: "Because we divide equally."

He said: "Then why is there no coarse or harsh one among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness."

He said: "Then what has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice."

He said: "Then why do you not laugh?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness."

He said: "Then why do you not grieve or become angry?" They said: "Because since we existed we have prepared ourselves for trials, we have loved them, and we have eagerly sought them."

He said: "Then why do calamities not afflict you as they afflict people?" They said: "Because we rely on none but God, and we do not practise omens or stars."

He said: "And so you found your forefathers doing?" They said: "Yes. We found our forefathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, showing forbearance to those who acted ignorantly towards them, keeping their kinship ties, fulfilling their trusts, guarding the times of their prayers, keeping their covenants, and being truthful in their promises. By this God, mighty and majestic, set their affairs right and preserved them while they were alive. It was indeed due from God that He should make them successors in their descendants."

Qatadah related from Abu Rafi' from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through it every day until, when they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God, mighty and majestic, restores it stronger than it was. When their term is fulfilled and they dig until they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow, God willing.' It returns to them just as it was when they left it. They dig through it and come out upon the people and drink the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and the arrows return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God, mighty and majestic, sends a worm [[In the Isfahan copy: a worm. (Marginal note in the manuscript.)]] upon them in their necks, and they die." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and become sated from their flesh."

Mahmud ibn Qatadah related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say:

'Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out as God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿and they will swarm from every slope﴾ [Qur'an 21:96]. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their fortresses and cities, until the first of them pass by the river, one of the rivers of the earth, [and drink it].'"

Abu al-Haytham said: the Tigris. "They will drink until it becomes dry land. Those who come after them will pass by it and say: 'There was water in this place once.' When they prevail over the people of the earth they say: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them, and only the people of heaven remain.'"

He (ﷺ) said: "One of them will shake his spear and then hurl it toward the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a trial. While they are in that state, God, mighty and majestic, will send upon them worms like the locust's larva, and they will die like locusts die. In the morning the Muslims will hear no sound from them, and they will say: 'Is there any man who will sell himself for us, to go and see what these people have done?' A man from among them will go down, having become certain that he will be killed. He will find them dead, some upon others, and he will call out to his companions: 'Rejoice, for God, mighty and majestic, has spared you their enemy.' Then the Muslims will come out and send their livestock to graze among them, and they will have no pasture except their flesh, and it will swell upon it more than it swells upon any plant that has ever touched it."

Wahb said: "They used to come to the sea and drink its water, and eat its creatures. Then they would eat wood, trees, and whatever people they could seize. They could not reach Mecca, Medina, or Bayt al-Maqdis."

Concerning His saying, ﴿Shall we pay you a tribute?﴾: the people of Kufa read *kharājan* with an *alif*, while the rest read it without *alif*. The two are dialectal variants with one meaning.
